docstring: Nested finite histories generated by the diagonal construction.
name: GenLimit.Angluin.adversarialHistory
type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  {β : Sort u_2} →
    (M : List α → β) →
      (L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α) →
        (base : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α) →
          GenLimit.Generic.StreamIn base L →
            (∀ (xs : List α), GenLimit.Angluin.ListWithin xs L → GenLimit.Angluin.HasChangeExtension M L xs) →
              ℕ → GenLimit.Angluin.HistoryIn L

name: GenLimit.Angluin.adversarialHistory.eq_def
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Sort u_2} (M : List α → β) (L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α) (base : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α)
  (hbase : GenLimit.Generic.StreamIn base L)
  (hchange : ∀ (xs : List α), GenLimit.Angluin.ListWithin xs L → GenLimit.Angluin.HasChangeExtension M L xs) (x : ℕ),
  GenLimit.Angluin.adversarialHistory M L base hbase hchange x =
    match x with
    | 0 => ⟨[], ⋯⟩
    | n.succ =>
      GenLimit.Angluin.adversarialStep M L base hbase hchange n
        (GenLimit.Angluin.adversarialHistory M L base hbase hchange n)

type:

  GenLimit.Angluin.effectiveStageEligible F emit (List.ofFn xs) i = true ↔
    GenLimit.Angluin.stageContents emit i t ⊆ GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample xs ∧
      ↑(GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample xs) ⊆ F.language i

    (GenLimit.Angluin.effectiveStageEligible F emit (List.ofFn xs) i = true ↔
      GenLimit.Angluin.StageEligible F.language (GenLimit.Angluin.stageContents emit) (List.ofFn xs) i)

name: GenLimit.Angluin.emissionAccepted_computable
type: ∀ {emit : ℕ → ℕ → Option ℕ}, Computable₂ emit → Computable₂ (GenLimit.Angluin.emissionAccepted emit)

docstring:

already appeared in the data.
name: GenLimit.Angluin.emissionCheck

name: GenLimit.Angluin.emissionCheck_computable

name: GenLimit.Angluin.emissionCheck_eq_true_iff
type:
∀ (emit : ℕ → ℕ → Option ℕ) {t i : ℕ} (xs : Fin t → ℕ),
  GenLimit.Angluin.emissionCheck emit (List.ofFn xs) i = true ↔

docstring: Compatibility name for the shared stage-by-stage enumeration API.
name: GenLimit.Angluin.enumeratedSet

name: GenLimit.Angluin.eventually_all_lt
type: ∀ {P : ℕ → ℕ → Prop} {k : ℕ}, (∀ i < k, ∃ N, ∀ (t : ℕ), N ≤ t → P i t) → ∃ N, ∀ (t : ℕ), N ≤ t → ∀ i < k, P i t

docstring:
Every fixed lower index denoting a different language eventually fails one
of the two substantive stage tests.

If the target is not contained in the candidate, positive data eventually
exhibit a counterexample.  If the target is a proper subset of the candidate,
the candidate's tell-tale eventually emits an element outside the target.
name: GenLimit.Angluin.eventually_not_stageEligible_of_different_language
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {C : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageFamily α} {A : ℕ → ℕ → Finset α},
  GenLimit.Angluin.IsTellTaleApproximation C A →
    ∀ {z i : ℕ},
      C i ≠ C z →
        ∀ {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α},
          GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream (C z) →
            ∃ N, ∀ (t : ℕ), N ≤ t → ¬GenLimit.Angluin.StageEligible C A (GenLimit.textPrefix stream t) i

docstring: A fixed index denoting the target eventually passes the stage test.
name: GenLimit.Angluin.eventually_stageEligible_of_same_language
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {C : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageFamily α} {A : ℕ → ℕ → Finset α},
  GenLimit.Angluin.IsTellTaleApproximation C A →
    ∀ {z i : ℕ},
      C i = C z →
        ∀ {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α},
          GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream (C z) →
            ∃ N, ∀ (t : ℕ), N ≤ t → GenLimit.Angluin.StageEligible C A (GenLimit.textPrefix stream t) i

docstring:
If a finite-history learner converges on every exact presentation of a
language, then some finite history locks its output on every continuation
from that language.  Supplying the base presentation keeps this statement
independent of any particular enumeration theorem for the example type.
name: GenLimit.Angluin.exists_lockingSequence_of_converges_with_base
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : List α → β} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α} {base : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α},
  GenLimit.Generic.Presents base L →
    (∀ (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α),
        GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream L → ∃ j, GenLimit.StabilizesTo (fun t => M (GenLimit.textPrefix stream t)) j) →
      ∃ xs j, GenLimit.Angluin.IsLockingSequence M L xs j

docstring:
Every nonempty language over a countable example space has an exact
positive presentation.
name: GenLimit.Angluin.exists_presentation_of_nonempty
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [Countable α] {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  Set.Nonempty L → ∃ stream, GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream L

name: GenLimit.Angluin.exists_syntacticallyStabilizing
type:
∀ {M : GenLimit.Angluin.EffectiveIdentifier} {L : Set ℕ},
  L.Nonempty →
    (∀ (stream : ℕ → ℕ),
        GenLimit.Presents stream L → ∃ guess T, ∀ (t : ℕ), T ≤ t → M (GenLimit.textPrefix stream t) = guess) →
      ∃ history, GenLimit.Angluin.SyntacticallyStabilizing M L history

docstring:
A coded extension is accepted when it is not target-consistent, or when
it leaves the learner's current conjecture unchanged.

type: GenLimit.Angluin.EffectiveIndexedFamily → GenLimit.Angluin.EffectiveIdentifier → ℕ × List ℕ → ℕ → Bool

name: GenLimit.Angluin.extensionAccepted_computable
type:
∀ (F : GenLimit.Angluin.EffectiveIndexedFamily) {M : GenLimit.Angluin.EffectiveIdentifier},
  Computable M → Computable₂ (GenLimit.Angluin.extensionAccepted F M)

name: GenLimit.Angluin.extensionAccepted_eq_true_iff
type:
∀ (F : GenLimit.Angluin.EffectiveIndexedFamily) (M : GenLimit.Angluin.EffectiveIdentifier) (i : ℕ) (history : List ℕ)
  (code : ℕ),
  GenLimit.Angluin.extensionAccepted F M (i, history) code = true ↔
    GenLimit.Angluin.ListWithin (GenLimit.Angluin.decodedHistory code) (F.language i) →
      M (history ++ GenLimit.Angluin.decodedHistory code) = M history

docstring:

when the difference is empty. This function is used only in the finiteness
proof; the stage emitter below remains fully computable.

name: GenLimit.Angluin.firstDifference_eq_of_least

∀ {target candidate : Set ℕ} {x : ℕ},
  x ∈ target →
    x ∉ candidate → (∀ y < x, y ∈ target → y ∈ candidate) → GenLimit.Angluin.firstDifference target candidate = x

docstring: Compatibility name for the shared bounded least-witness search.

type: {α : Type u_1} → (α → ℕ → Bool) → α → ℕ → Option ℕ

name: GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue_computable
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Primcodable α] {p : α → ℕ → Bool}, Computable₂ p → Computable₂ (GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue p)

name: GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue_eq_none_iff
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (p : α → ℕ → Bool) (a : α) (n : ℕ), GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue p a n = none ↔ ∀ i < n, p a i = false

name: GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue_le_of_true
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {p : α → ℕ → Bool} {a : α} {n i j : ℕ},
  GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue p a n = some j → i < n → p a i = true → j ≤ i

name: GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue_spec
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {p : α → ℕ → Bool} {a : α} {n i : ℕ},
  GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue p a n = some i → i < n ∧ p a i = true ∧ ∀ j < i, p a j = false

name: GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue_succ
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (p : α → ℕ → Bool) (a : α) (n : ℕ),
  GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue p a (n + 1) =
    match GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue p a n with
    | some i => some i
    | none => if p a n = true then some n else none

name: GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue_zero
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (p : α → ℕ → Bool) (a : α), GenLimit.Angluin.firstTrue p a 0 = none

name: GenLimit.Angluin.hasChangeExtension_of_not_locking

Theorem 4.2 with the paper's literal `k ≥ 3` indexing.
name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.Results.theorem_4_2_order_robust
type:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  3 ≤ k →
    ∃ K langs target,
      Function.Injective langs ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), (langs i).Infinite) ∧
          langs target = K.carrier ∧
            ∀ (G : GenLimit.BoundedMemory.MemorylessSetGenerator ℕ),
              GenLimit.BoundedMemory.IsFinitelyRepeatingMemorylessGenerator G (Set.range langs) →
                ∀ (stream : ℕ → ℕ),
                  GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream K.carrier →
                    Function.Injective stream →
                      (∃ T, ∀ (t : ℕ), T ≤ t → K.lowerDensity (G (stream t)) = 0) ∧
                        ∀ (σ : ℝ), 0 < σ → ¬∃ᶠ (t : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, σ ≤ K.lowerDensity (G (stream t))

type:
∀ {n : ℕ},
  2 ≤ n →
    ∀ (G : GenLimit.BoundedMemory.MemorylessSetGenerator ℕ),
      GenLimit.BoundedMemory.IsFinitelyRepeatingMemorylessGenerator G
          (Set.range (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.spernerHardFamily n)) →
        ∀ (stream : ℕ → ℕ),
          GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream GenLimit.BoundedMemory.spernerTargetOrder.carrier →
            Function.Injective stream →
              ∃ T,

docstring:

reciprocal middle-layer width on the fixed identity presentation.

The source indexes a window by its final position.  Here `start` is its first
position; the two eventual formulations differ by the fixed shift `W - 1`.
name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.eventually_windowHard_upperDensity_bound
type:
∀ {n W : ℕ},
  2 ≤ n →
    0 < W →
      ∀ (G : GenLimit.BoundedMemory.WindowSetGenerator ℕ W),
        (∀ (a : Fin (n + 1)),
            GenLimit.BoundedMemory.IsRepetitionFreeWindowGeneratorOn G (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.windowHardFamily n a)) →
          ∃ T,
            ∀ (start : ℕ),
              T ≤ start →
                GenLimit.BoundedMemory.windowHardTargetOrder.upperDensity
                    (G.output (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.identityWindow start W)) ≤
                  1 / ↑(n.choose (n / 2))

docstring: Exact finite-exception conclusion of source Lemma 4.11.

type:

  0 < W →
    ∀ {L : Set α},
      L.Infinite →
        ∀ {G : GenLimit.BoundedMemory.WindowSetGenerator α W},
          GenLimit.BoundedMemory.IsRepetitionFreeWindowGeneratorOn G L →
            ∃ B,
              ↑B ⊆ L ∧
                ∀ (w : GenLimit.BoundedMemory.DistinctWindow α W), (∀ (i : Fin W), ↑w i ∈ L ∧ ↑w i ∉ B) → G.output w ⊆ L

docstring:
Lemma 4.12 with the source's quantifier order.

For each `k`, the family, target, density order, and repetition-free exact
presentation are fixed before the window width and generator are chosen.
The family is represented by an injective `Fin k` indexing, recording that it
has exactly `k` distinct infinite languages.
name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.lemma_4_12_single_hard_instance
type:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  2 ≤ k →
    ∃ K langs target stream,
      ∃ (hstream : Function.Injective stream),
        Function.Injective langs ∧
          (∀ (a : Fin k), (langs a).Infinite) ∧
            langs target = K.carrier ∧
              GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream K.carrier ∧
                ∀ (W : ℕ),
                  0 < W →
                    ∀ (G : GenLimit.BoundedMemory.WindowSetGenerator ℕ W),
                      (∀ (a : Fin k), GenLimit.BoundedMemory.IsRepetitionFreeWindowGeneratorOn G (langs a)) →
                        ∃ T,
                          ∀ (start : ℕ),
                            T ≤ start →
                              K.upperDensity (G.output (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.windowAt stream hstream start W)) ≤
                                1 / ↑((k - 1).choose ((k - 1) / 2))

docstring:
Lemma 4.3, with the paper's actual `liminf` lower density.

After a finite exceptional time, every output is contained in the unique
partition piece containing the current example and hence has lower density
at most the maximum lower density of a piece.  Uniqueness is not needed for
the inequality, so the proof consumes only coverage, although the literal
partition predicate retains pairwise disjointness.
name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.lemma_4_3_lower_density_bound_from_partition
type:
∀ {m : ℕ} (K : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) (pieces : Fin (m + 1) → Set ℕ),
  GenLimit.BoundedMemory.IsFinitePartition pieces K.carrier →
    (∀ (i : Fin (m + 1)), (pieces i).Infinite) →
      ∀ (G : GenLimit.BoundedMemory.MemorylessSetGenerator ℕ),
        (∀ (i : Fin (m + 1)), GenLimit.BoundedMemory.IsRepetitionFreeMemorylessGeneratorOn G (pieces i)) →
          ∀ (stream : ℕ → ℕ),
            GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream K.carrier →
              Function.Injective stream →
                ∃ T,
                  ∀ (t : ℕ),
                    T ≤ t → K.lowerDensity (G (stream t)) ≤ GenLimit.BoundedMemory.maximumPartitionLowerDensity K pieces

docstring:
Lemma 4.4, exactly at the paper's ordered-`liminf` level.

Any canonically ordered countably infinite language is partitioned into
`m ≥ 2` pairwise-disjoint infinite cells, and every cell has lower density
zero in that same canonical ordering.
name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.lemma_4_4_zero_lower_density_partition
type:
∀ (K : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) (m : ℕ),
  2 ≤ m →
    ∃ pieces,
      (∀ (i j : Fin m), i ≠ j → Disjoint (pieces i) (pieces j)) ∧
        ⋃ i, pieces i = K.carrier ∧ (∀ (i : Fin m), (pieces i).Infinite) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin m), K.lowerDensity (pieces i) = 0

docstring:
Lemma 4.7 with its literal quantifier order and upper-density value.

The family is represented by an injective `Fin k` indexing, which formally
records that the collection has exactly `k` distinct infinite languages.
Index `0` is the target.
name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.lemma_4_7_sperner_hard_instance
type:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  2 ≤ k →
    ∃ K langs target,
      Function.Injective langs ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), (langs i).Infinite) ∧
          langs target = K.carrier ∧
            ∀ (G : GenLimit.BoundedMemory.MemorylessSetGenerator ℕ),
              GenLimit.BoundedMemory.IsFinitelyRepeatingMemorylessGenerator G (Set.range langs) →
                ∀ (stream : ℕ → ℕ),
                  GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream K.carrier →
                    Function.Injective stream →
                      ∃ T, ∀ (t : ℕ), T ≤ t → K.upperDensity (G (stream t)) ≤ 1 / ↑((k - 1).choose ((k - 1) / 2))

docstring:
Lemma 4.8: the canonical memoryless intersection generator both
generates every member of a finite family under finitely repeating
enumerations and achieves the exact reciprocal-Sperner upper-density bound
infinitely often on every target.
name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.lemma_4_8_sperner_achievability
type:
∀ {n : ℕ},
  1 ≤ n →
    ∀ (langs : Fin (n + 1) → Set ℕ),
      (∀ (i : Fin (n + 1)), (langs i).Infinite) →
        ∃ G,
          GenLimit.BoundedMemory.IsFinitelyRepeatingMemorylessGenerator G (Set.range langs) ∧
            ∀ (target : Fin (n + 1)) (K : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage),
              K.carrier = langs target →
                ∀ (stream : ℕ → ℕ),
                  GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream K.carrier →
                    GenLimit.BoundedMemory.FinitelyRepeating stream →
                      ∃ᶠ (t : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 1 / ↑(n.choose (n / 2)) ≤ K.upperDensity (G (stream t))

docstring:
Lemma A.3: every finite family of infinite languages admits pairwise
disjoint infinite cofinal coding cells contained in the corresponding
languages.
name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.lemma_A_3
type:
∀ {N : ℕ} (langs : Fin (N + 1) → Set ℕ),
  (∀ (i : Fin (N + 1)), (langs i).Infinite) →
    ∃ cells,
      (∀ (i : Fin (N + 1)), (cells i).Infinite ∧ cells i ⊆ langs i) ∧
        Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint cells) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin (N + 1)) (x : ℕ), ∃ y ∈ cells i, x < y

name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.paperZeroDensityPiece_lowerDensity

∀ (K : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) {m : ℕ},

∀ (K : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) (m : ℕ) (i j : Fin m),

docstring:
At the end of a block owned by another cell, all occurrences of this
cell lie before the start of that block.  This is the finite-count estimate
in the proof of Lemma 4.4.
name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.prefixCount_paperZeroDensityPiece_le
type:
∀ (K : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) {m : ℕ} (i : Fin m) {t : ℕ},
  t % m ≠ ↑i →
    K.prefixCount (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.paperZeroDensityPiece K m i)
        (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.paperBlockBoundary (t + 1)) ≤
      GenLimit.BoundedMemory.paperBlockBoundary t

name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.prefixCount_roundRobin_lower
type:
∀ {N : ℕ},
  0 < N →
    ∀ (i : Fin N) (n : ℕ),
      n / N ≤ GenLimit.BoundedMemory.spernerTargetOrder.prefixCount (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.roundRobinPiece i) n

name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.prefixCount_roundRobin_upper
type:
∀ {N : ℕ},
  0 < N →
    ∀ (i : Fin N) (n : ℕ),
      GenLimit.BoundedMemory.spernerTargetOrder.prefixCount (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.roundRobinPiece i) n ≤ n / N + 1

name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.prefixRatio_paperZeroDensityPiece_le
type:
∀ (K : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) {m : ℕ} (i : Fin m) {t : ℕ},
  t % m ≠ ↑i →
    K.prefixRatio (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.paperZeroDensityPiece K m i)
        (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.paperBlockBoundary (t + 1)) ≤
      1 / (↑t + 1)

name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.prefixRatio_roundRobin_bounds
type:
∀ {N : ℕ},
  0 < N →
    ∀ (i : Fin N) {n : ℕ},
      0 < n →
        1 / ↑N - 1 / ↑n ≤
            GenLimit.BoundedMemory.spernerTargetOrder.prefixRatio (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.roundRobinPiece i) n ∧
          GenLimit.BoundedMemory.spernerTargetOrder.prefixRatio (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.roundRobinPiece i) n ≤
            1 / ↑N + 1 / ↑n

docstring:
Proposition 5.1: the literal three-language family cannot be identified
exactly by a last-guess learner whose only states are its three hypothesis
indices.  The obstruction already uses finitely repeating presentations.
name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.proposition_5_1
type:
(∀ (i : Fin 3), (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.exactObstructionLanguages i).Infinite) ∧
  Function.Injective GenLimit.BoundedMemory.exactObstructionLanguages ∧
    ¬GenLimit.BoundedMemory.IncrementallyExactlyIdentifiableOnFinitelyRepeating
        GenLimit.BoundedMemory.exactObstructionLanguages

name: GenLimit.BoundedMemory.proposition_A_2
type:
∀ {α : Type u} [Countable α] {T : Set α},
  T.Infinite →
    ∀ {a b c : α},
      a ≠ b →
        a ≠ c →
          b ≠ c →
            a ∉ T →
              b ∉ T →
                c ∉ T →
                  ¬GenLimit.BoundedMemory.IncrementallyIndexGenerableOnFinitelyRepeating
                      (GenLimit.BoundedMemory.appendixTriangleLanguages T a b c)

            ∀ (G : GenLimit.BoundedMemory.MemorylessSetGenerator ℕ),

    GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.CompletionDrivenStep A current → GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.PartialTwoLanguageAssignment

GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.CompletionDrivenStep.execution
GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.CompletionDrivenStep.mk
type:
{A : GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.TwoLanguageMembershipAlgorithm} →
  {current : GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.FiniteDiagonalStage} →
    (newInput : ℕ) →
      current.assignment newInput = none →
        (commonAssignment : GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.PartialTwoLanguageAssignment) →
          commonAssignment = GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.assignCommon current.assignment newInput →
            (temporaryLeft temporaryRight : Set ℕ) →
              temporaryLeft.Infinite →
                temporaryRight.Infinite →
                  GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.LanguagePairRealizes commonAssignment temporaryLeft temporaryRight →
                    temporaryLeft ∩ temporaryRight ⊆
                        GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.partialAssignmentCommon commonAssignment →
                      (rounds : List GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.TwoLanguageRound) →
                        (output : ℕ) →
                          GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.ExecutionValid A temporaryLeft temporaryRight
                              (current.inputs ++ [newInput]) rounds →
                            (∃ (hlast : current.inputs.length < rounds.length),
                                (rounds.get ⟨current.inputs.length, hlast⟩).2.2 = output) →
                              (queryAssignment : GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.PartialTwoLanguageAssignment) →
                                queryAssignment =
                                    GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.recordExecutionAnswers commonAssignment temporaryLeft
                                      temporaryRight rounds →
                                  (GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.partialAssignmentDomain queryAssignment).Finite →
                                    GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.PartialAssignmentDecidesExecution queryAssignment
                                        rounds →
                                      GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.LanguagePairRealizes queryAssignment temporaryLeft
                                          temporaryRight →
                                        GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.partialAssignmentCommon queryAssignment ⊆
                                            GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.partialAssignmentCommon commonAssignment →
                                          (next : GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.FiniteDiagonalStage) →
                                            next.inputs = current.inputs ++ [newInput] →
                                              next.assignment =
                                                  GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.recordOutput queryAssignment output →
                                                GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.AssignmentExtends current.assignment
                                                    next.assignment →
                                                  GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.CompletionDrivenStep A current

docstring:
The faithful finite endgame of Theorem 7.  Once two exact presentations
share a prefix whose sample is above both non-uniform thresholds, an output on
that prefix must be fresh and belong to both languages.  The two membership
conclusions come from two separate applications of the guarantee.
name: GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.nonuniformGuarantee_commonPrefix_output
type:
∀ {A : GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.TwoLanguageMembershipAlgorithm} {L₀ L₁ : Set ℕ},
  GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.NonuniformTwoLanguageMembershipGuarantee A L₀ L₁ →
    ∃ d₀ d₁,
      ∀ (stream₀ stream₁ : GenLimit.Generic.Stream ℕ) (t z : ℕ),
        GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream₀ L₀ →
          GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream₁ L₁ →
            (∀ k < t + 1, stream₀ k = stream₁ k) →
              GenLimit.CharikarPabbaraju.MembershipExecutionOutputsAt A L₀ L₁ stream₀ t z →
                max d₀ d₁ ≤ (GenLimit.Generic.sample stream₀ (t + 1)).card →
                  z ∈ (L₀ ∩ L₁) \ ↑(GenLimit.Generic.sample stream₀ (t + 1))

docstring:

    (∀ h ∈ family, h ∈ 𝓗) →
      GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.IsSharedPresentation stream family →
        GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.IsFiniteFamilyIntersection family core →
          ¬GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.ContrastivelyGeneratable 𝓗

Theorem 5.4, exact quantitative finite-bound form: a uniform generator
works after `d+1` distinct unordered edges exactly when every hollow edge set
has cardinality at most `d`.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.Results.theorem_5_4_quantitative
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [Nonempty α] (𝓗 : Set (Set α)) (d : ℕ),
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.UniformlyContrastivelyGeneratableAt 𝓗 (d + 1) ↔
    GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.ContrastiveClosureDimensionAtMost 𝓗 d

---

Theorem 5.4's sharp sample-complexity statement.  If the finite closure
dimension has exact value `d`, then `d+1` is the least positive
distinct-edge threshold for a uniform contrastive generator.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.Results.theorem_5_4_sharp_sample_complexity
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [Nonempty α] {𝓗 : Set (Set α)} {d : ℕ},
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.ContrastiveClosureDimensionEquals 𝓗 d →
    GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.IsLeastPositiveUniformThreshold 𝓗 (d + 1)

an increasing union of classes of finite contrastive closure dimension.

∀ {α : Type u_1} [Nonempty α] (𝓗 : Set (Set α)),
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.NonuniformlyContrastivelyGeneratable 𝓗 ↔
    ∃ classes,
      GenLimit.Generic.IsNondecreasingCover 𝓗 classes ∧
        ∀ (n : ℕ), GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.FiniteContrastiveClosureDimension (classes n)

class separates corrupted contrastive identification from corrupted text
identification, while the `(k+1)`-block class gives the reverse separation.

        ¬GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.KTextIdentifiable k GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.coSingletonFamily) ∧
      GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.KTextIdentifiable k (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.robustBlockFamily k) ∧
        ¬GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.KContrastivelyIdentifiable k
            (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.robustBlockFamily k)

docstring:
The simulated contrastive prefix in Lemma 4.6.  Every positive example
is paired with the least domain point absent from the whole current prefix.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.syntheticContrastiveHistory
type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [Infinite α] →
    (enumerate : ℕ → α) →
      Function.Surjective enumerate → {t : ℕ} → (Fin t → α) → Fin t → GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.Edge α

name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.syntheticContrastiveHistory_eq_fixed
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (enumerate : ℕ → α) (henumerate : Function.Surjective enumerate)
  {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {t k : ℕ},
  (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.firstUnseenIndex enumerate henumerate fun i => stream ↑i) = k →
    ∀ (hne : ∀ (i : Fin t), stream ↑i ≠ enumerate k),
      (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.syntheticContrastiveHistory enumerate henumerate fun i => stream ↑i) = fun i =>
        { left := stream ↑i, right := enumerate k, ne := ⋯ }

      GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.IsContrastivePresentation stream h →
        ∀ (t : ℕ),
          h ∈ GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.edgeVersionSpace 𝓗 (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.streamPrefix stream t)

∀ {α : Type u_1} (h g : Set α),
  h ⊆ GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.commonVertices h g ↔
    ((GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.bothPositive h g).Nonempty →
        (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.bothNegative h g).Nonempty) ∧
      ((GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.hOnly h g).Nonempty → (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.gOnly h g).Nonempty)

docstring:
Theorem 4.7, conditions (i) and (iii).  Together with
`theorem_4_7_identifier_equivalence` and
`theorem_4_7_geometric_equivalence`, this is the source's complete
three-way characterization.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_4_7
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [Nonempty α] [Countable α] [Infinite α] (F : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageFamily α),
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.AllProperNontrivial F →
    (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.ContrastivelyIdentifiable F ↔
      GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.TextIdentifiable F ∧
        GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.IncomparablePairsOverlap (Set.range F))

docstring:
Theorem 4.7(ii) ↔ (iii), after replacing non-eliminability by the
equivalent common-crossing coverage relation from Proposition 4.2.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_4_7_geometric_equivalence
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (𝓗 : Set (Set α)),
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.NonEliminabilityContained 𝓗 ↔ GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.IncomparablePairsOverlap 𝓗

docstring:
Theorem 4.7, conditions (i) and (ii), including actual existence of the
contrastive identifier.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_4_7_identifier_equivalence
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [Nonempty α] [Countable α] [Infinite α] (F : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageFamily α),
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.AllProperNontrivial F →
    (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.ContrastivelyIdentifiable F ↔
      GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.TextIdentifiable F ∧
        GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.NonEliminabilityContained (Set.range F))

docstring:
The other half of Theorem 5.14, together with the strict
`CtrGen ⊂ TxtGen` witness used in Theorem 5.13.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_5_13_5_14_disjoint_witness
type:
GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.TextIdentifiable GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.disjointFamily ∧
  GenLimit.Generic.GeneratableInLimit (Set.range GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.disjointFamily) ∧
    ¬GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.ContrastivelyGeneratable (Set.range GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.disjointFamily)

docstring:
A theorem-level witness for

name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_5_13_5_14_punctured_witness

GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.ContrastivelyGeneratable (Set.range GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.puncturedFamily) ∧
  ¬GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.TextIdentifiable GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.puncturedFamily ∧
    ¬GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.ContrastivelyIdentifiable GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.puncturedFamily

docstring:
Theorem 5.4, qualitative form: uniform contrastive generation is
equivalent to finiteness of the contrastive closure dimension.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_5_4
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [Nonempty α] (𝓗 : Set (Set α)),
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.UniformlyContrastivelyGeneratable 𝓗 ↔
    GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.FiniteContrastiveClosureDimension 𝓗

docstring:
Theorem 5.4, exact quantitative finite-bound form: a uniform generator
works after `d+1` distinct unordered edges exactly when every hollow edge set
has cardinality at most `d`.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_5_4_quantitative
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [Nonempty α] (𝓗 : Set (Set α)) (d : ℕ),
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.UniformlyContrastivelyGeneratableAt 𝓗 (d + 1) ↔
    GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.ContrastiveClosureDimensionAtMost 𝓗 d

docstring:
Theorem 5.4's sharp sample-complexity statement.  If the finite closure
dimension has exact value `d`, then `d+1` is the least positive
distinct-edge threshold for a uniform contrastive generator.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_5_4_sharp_sample_complexity
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [Nonempty α] {𝓗 : Set (Set α)} {d : ℕ},
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.ContrastiveClosureDimensionEquals 𝓗 d →
    GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.IsLeastPositiveUniformThreshold 𝓗 (d + 1)

docstring:
Theorem 5.5: non-uniform contrastive generation is equivalent to being
an increasing union of classes of finite contrastive closure dimension.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_5_5
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [Nonempty α] (𝓗 : Set (Set α)),
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.NonuniformlyContrastivelyGeneratable 𝓗 ↔
    ∃ classes,
      GenLimit.Generic.IsNondecreasingCover 𝓗 classes ∧
        ∀ (n : ℕ), GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.FiniteContrastiveClosureDimension (classes n)

docstring:
Necessity in Theorem 5.5: target-dependent thresholds stratify the class
into a nondecreasing cover of finite closure dimension.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_5_5_necessity
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {𝓗 : Set (Set α)},
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.NonuniformlyContrastivelyGeneratable 𝓗 →
    ∃ classes,
      GenLimit.Generic.IsNondecreasingCover 𝓗 classes ∧
        ∀ (n : ℕ), GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.FiniteContrastiveClosureDimension (classes n)

docstring:
Sufficiency in Theorem 5.5.  The proof uses one closure generator at the
largest active component and monotonicity of the cover to retain the target.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_5_5_sufficiency
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [Nonempty α] {𝓗 : Set (Set α)} {classes : ℕ → Set (Set α)},
  GenLimit.Generic.IsNondecreasingCover 𝓗 classes →
    (∀ (n : ℕ), GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.FiniteContrastiveClosureDimension (classes n)) →
      GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.NonuniformlyContrastivelyGeneratable 𝓗

docstring:
Theorem 6.5: the co-singleton class is not identifiable from texts with
even one corrupted occurrence.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_6_5
type: ¬GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.KTextIdentifiable 1 GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.coSingletonFamily

docstring:
Theorem 6.6: one budget-independent absence-count identifier recovers
every co-singleton target under every finite contrastive corruption budget.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_6_6
type:
GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.FinitelyCorruptionContrastivelyIdentifiable
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.coSingletonFamily

docstring:
Theorem 6.8: for every positive corruption budget, the co-singleton
class separates corrupted contrastive identification from corrupted text
identification, while the `(k+1)`-block class gives the reverse separation.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.theorem_6_8
type:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  1 ≤ k →
    (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.KContrastivelyIdentifiable k GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.coSingletonFamily ∧
        ¬GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.KTextIdentifiable k GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.coSingletonFamily) ∧
      GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.KTextIdentifiable k (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.robustBlockFamily k) ∧
        ¬GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.KContrastivelyIdentifiable k
            (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.robustBlockFamily k)

docstring:
Every prefix absence of the true co-singleton center is a corrupted
observation.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.trueCenter_absence_indices_subset_bad
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] (stream : ℕ → GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.Edge α) (s : α) (t : ℕ),
  {i ∈ Finset.range t | ¬GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.Incident s (stream i)} ⊆
    {i ∈ Finset.range t |
      ¬GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.Crosses (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.coSingletonSupport s) (stream i)}

docstring: The true center eventually belongs to the observed candidate set.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.trueCenter_eventually_seen
type:
∀ {k s : ℕ} {stream : ℕ → GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.Edge ℕ},
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.IsKCorruptedContrastivePresentation k stream
      (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.coSingletonSupport s) →
    ∃ T,
      ∀ (t : ℕ),
        T ≤ t → s ∈ GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.seenEndpoints (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.streamPrefix stream t)

docstring:
The true center's absence count is bounded by the declared corruption
budget at every time.
name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.trueCenter_streamAbsenceCount_le
type:
∀ {k s t : ℕ} {stream : ℕ → GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.Edge ℕ},
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.IsKCorruptedContrastivePresentation k stream
      (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.coSingletonSupport s) →
    GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.streamAbsenceCount stream s t ≤ k

name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.uniformThreshold_mono

  d ≤ d' →
    GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.UniformlyContrastivelyGeneratesAt G 𝓗 d →
      GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.UniformlyContrastivelyGeneratesAt G 𝓗 d'

{α : Type u_1} →
  {h g : Set α} →
    h ∪ g ⊆ GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.commonVertices h g →
      (x : α) → x ∈ h ∪ g → GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.Edge α

name: GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.unionCoveringEdge_spec
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {h g : Set α} (hcover : h ∪ g ⊆ GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.commonVertices h g) (x : α)
  (hx : x ∈ h ∪ g),
  GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.CommonCrossing h g (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.unionCoveringEdge hcover x hx) ∧
    GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.Incident x (GenLimit.ContrastiveGeneration.unionCoveringEdge hcover x hx)

docstring:
Definition 5.1's edge-induced closure, with the paper's empty-version
space convention.

Lemma 3.16 together with the standard novelty guarantees of the semantic
patient-scope machine.
name: GenLimit.DenseGeneration.Results.lemma_3_16
type:
∀ (O : GenLimit.OracleFamily) {stream : ℕ → ℕ} {E : GenLimit.Language} {z : ℕ},
  GenLimit.Presents stream E →
    Set.Infinite E →
      E ⊆ O.language z →
        ∃ T,
          ∀ (t : ℕ),
            T ≤ t →
              GenLimit.PatientMachine.output (GenLimit.PartialEnumeration.closure O) stream t ∈ O.language z ∧
                (∀ s ≤ t, stream s ≠ GenLimit.PatientMachine.output (GenLimit.PartialEnumeration.closure O) stream t) ∧
                  ∀ s < t,
                    GenLimit.PatientMachine.output (GenLimit.PartialEnumeration.closure O) stream s ≠
                      GenLimit.PatientMachine.output (GenLimit.PartialEnumeration.closure O) stream t

        GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.SourceSetQueryGeneratable (⋃ i, classes i))

generators: a fresh successful generator may have a presentation with no

            (GenLimit.textPrefix GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.NoFeedbackLockingGap.basePresentation n)

type:

docstring:

scheduled query from that row so far was positive.
name: GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverOneQuery_truthful_rowPasses_iff
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Countable α] {targets : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α}
  (inner : GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.CountableInnerCover targets) (L : Set α) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α)

  GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.OneQueryRowPasses t
      (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.positiveSequenceOneQueryFeedback
        (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverOneQueryStrategy inner) L stream (t + 1))
      i ↔

          GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverOneQueryPoint inner r ∈ L

type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Countable α] {targets : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α}

type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Countable α] {targets : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α}

        (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverSourceElementStrategy inner samples bits) ≤
      GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceCanonicalRank x

docstring:
Every index below the least good cover is eventually rejected, so the
cover-search phase reaches that least good index.
name: GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverSourceElement_eventually_reaches
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Countable α] {targets : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α}
  (inner : GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.CountableInnerCover targets) (target : Set α) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α),
  GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream target →
    ∀ (k : ℕ),
      inner.cover k ⊆ target →
        (∀ i < k, ¬inner.cover i ⊆ target) →
          ∃ T,
            0 < T ∧
              GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceElementPhase
                  (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverSourceElementStrategy inner) target stream T =
                k

docstring:
If phase `i` is still active after every lower-ranked positive member of
cover `i` has appeared, the next proposal is the least negative witness.
name: GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverSourceElement_false_at_exposed_phase
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Countable α] {targets : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α}
  (inner : GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.CountableInnerCover targets) (target : Set α) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α),
  Set.range stream ⊆ target →
    ∀ {i t : ℕ},
      GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceElementPhase (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverSourceElementStrategy inner)
            target stream t =
          i →
        ∀ (hbad : ¬inner.cover i ⊆ target),
          (∀ x ∈ inner.cover i,
              GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceCanonicalRank x <
                  GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceCanonicalRank
                    (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceFirst (inner.cover i \ target) ⋯) →
                x ∈ GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.streamPrefix stream t) →
            GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceElementReply target (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.streamPrefix stream t)
                (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceElementOutput
                  (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverSourceElementStrategy inner) target
                  (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.streamPrefix stream t)) =
              false

docstring:
Once the active index is a cover contained in the target, its next bit is
positive and the phase remains fixed.
name: GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverSourceElement_good_phase_stays
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Countable α] {targets : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α}
  (inner : GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.CountableInnerCover targets) (target : Set α) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α)
  {k t : ℕ},
  0 < t →
    GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceElementPhase (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverSourceElementStrategy inner) target
          stream t =
        k →
      inner.cover k ⊆ target →
        GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceElementPhase (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverSourceElementStrategy inner)
            target stream (t + 1) =
          k

docstring: The cover search can never pass the least cover contained in the target.
name: GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverSourceElement_phase_le_good
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Countable α] {targets : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α}
  (inner : GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.CountableInnerCover targets) (target : Set α) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α)

  inner.cover k ⊆ target →
    ∀ (t : ℕ),
      GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceElementPhase (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.innerCoverSourceElementStrategy inner)
          target stream t ≤
        k

type:

              GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceElementSelfOutput strategy seed

                (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.sourceElementSelfHistory strategy seed

docstring:

the target, then remains there.

type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Countable α] {targets : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α}
  (inner : GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.CountableInnerCover targets) (target : Set α) (m : ℕ),
  GenLimit.Support.infiniteEnumeration (inner.cover m) ⋯ 0 ∈ target →
    (∀ i < m, GenLimit.Support.infiniteEnumeration (inner.cover i) ⋯ 0 ∉ target) →
      ∀ (t : ℕ), GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.zeroExampleMistakePhase inner target t = min t m

name: GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.zeroExampleMistakePhase_succ
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Countable α] {targets : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α}
  (inner : GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.CountableInnerCover targets) (target : Set α) (t : ℕ),
  GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.zeroExampleMistakePhase inner target (t + 1) =
    GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.zeroExampleMistakePhase inner target t +
      List.count false
        [GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.membershipAnswer target
            (GenLimit.Support.infiniteEnumeration
              (inner.cover (GenLimit.FeedbackQueries.zeroExampleMistakePhase inner target t)) ⋯ 0)]

{α : Type u_1} →
  (gen : GenLimit.Generic.SetGenerator α) → GenLimit.Generic.IsInfiniteSetGenerator gen → GenLimit.Generic.Generator α

name: GenLimit.Generic.elementGeneratorOfSet_mem
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (gen : GenLimit.Generic.SetGenerator α) (hinfinite : GenLimit.Generic.IsInfiniteSetGenerator gen)
  (t : ℕ) (samples : Fin t → α), GenLimit.Generic.elementGeneratorOfSet gen hinfinite t samples ∈ gen t samples

docstring: The value map of a finset's canonical `Fin` enumeration is injective.
name: GenLimit.Generic.equivFin_symm_value_injective
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (S : Finset α), Function.Injective fun i => ↑(S.equivFin.symm i)

docstring:
If every reached size can be crossed exactly, a property that holds
eventually after reaching exact size `d` also holds after reaching any larger
exact size.
name: GenLimit.Generic.eventualAtExactSize_mono
type:
∀ {size : ℕ → ℕ} {good : ℕ → Prop} {d n : ℕ},
  (∀ {t k : ℕ}, k ≤ size t → ∃ r ≤ t, size r = k) →
    d ≤ n → (∀ (t : ℕ), size t = d → ∀ (s : ℕ), t ≤ s → good s) → ∀ (t : ℕ), size t = n → ∀ (s : ℕ), t ≤ s → good s

name: GenLimit.Generic.eventually_mem_sample_of_presents
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream L → ∀ {x : α}, x ∈ L → ∃ T, ∀ (t : ℕ), T ≤ t → x ∈ GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t

name: GenLimit.Generic.exists_closure_witness_card_eq
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α},
  GenLimit.Generic.HasInfiniteClosureDimension H → ∀ (d : ℕ), ∃ S, S.card = d ∧ GenLimit.Generic.IsClosureWitness H S

docstring:
If a finite prefix contains at least `k` distinct observations, some
earlier prefix contains exactly `k`.
name: GenLimit.Generic.exists_sample_card_eq_of_le
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {t k : ℕ},
  k ≤ (GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t).card → ∃ r ≤ t, (GenLimit.Generic.sample stream r).card = k

docstring:
An exact presentation of an infinite language passes through every finite
number of distinct observations.
name: GenLimit.Generic.exists_sample_card_eq_of_presents_infinite
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream L → Set.Infinite L → ∀ (d : ℕ), ∃ t, (GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t).card = d

name: GenLimit.Generic.exists_sample_card_ge_of_presents_infinite
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream L → Set.Infinite L → ∀ (d : ℕ), ∃ t, d ≤ (GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t).card

name: GenLimit.Generic.exists_violationsAtMost_of_finitelyManyViolations
type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {stream : ℕ → α} {Acceptable : α → Prop},
  GenLimit.Generic.FinitelyManyViolations stream Acceptable → ∃ n, GenLimit.Generic.ViolationsAtMost stream Acceptable n

name: GenLimit.Generic.finite_closure_dimension_iff_not_infinite
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α},
  GenLimit.Generic.HasFiniteClosureDimension H ↔ ¬GenLimit.Generic.HasInfiniteClosureDimension H

docstring:
Every finite language class has finite positive closure dimension.

This is paper-independent finite-class infrastructure.  The proof takes the
maximum cardinality of the finite intersections arising from subcollections
of `H`; a larger consistent sample must therefore have infinite common core.
name: GenLimit.Generic.finite_language_class_has_finite_closure_dimension
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α}, Set.Finite H → GenLimit.Generic.HasFiniteClosureDimension H

docstring: The unbounded finite variants likewise agree for injective streams.
name: GenLimit.Generic.finite_valuesOutside_iff_finitelyManyViolations_of_injective
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  Function.Injective stream →
    ((Set.range stream \ L).Finite ↔ GenLimit.Generic.FinitelyManyViolations stream fun x => x ∈ L)

name: GenLimit.Generic.finitelyManyViolations_of_violationsAtMost
type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {stream : ℕ → α} {Acceptable : α → Prop} {n : ℕ},
  GenLimit.Generic.ViolationsAtMost stream Acceptable n → GenLimit.Generic.FinitelyManyViolations stream Acceptable

name: GenLimit.Generic.finset_eventually_subset_sample
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream L → ∀ (S : Finset α), ↑S ⊆ L → ∃ T, S ⊆ GenLimit.Generic.sample stream T

docstring:
Choose a fresh point from the language named by the learner's current
index guess.
name: GenLimit.Generic.freshFromIndexGuess
type:
{α : Type u_1} →
  (F : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageFamily α) →
    (∀ (i : ℕ), Set.Infinite (F i)) → GenLimit.Learner α ℕ → GenLimit.Generic.Generator α

name: GenLimit.Generic.freshFromIndexGuess_spec
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (F : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageFamily α) (hInfinite : ∀ (i : ℕ), Set.Infinite (F i))
  (M : GenLimit.Learner α ℕ) {t : ℕ} (history : Fin t → α),
  GenLimit.Generic.freshFromIndexGuess F hInfinite M t history ∈ F (M (List.ofFn history)) ∧
    GenLimit.Generic.freshFromIndexGuess F hInfinite M t history ∉ GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample history

docstring:
The stream that follows a finite history and then repeats a fallback
value forever.
name: GenLimit.Generic.historyThenFallback
type: {α : Type u_1} → List α → α → GenLimit.Generic.Stream α

docstring:
The range-based definition is equivalent to naming the infinite set
presented by the stream. This is the formulation used by Papers 15 and 39.
name: GenLimit.Generic.infinitePartialPresentation_iff_exists_presented_subset
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α) (K : GenLimit.Generic.Language α),
  GenLimit.Generic.InfinitePartialPresentation stream K ↔
    ∃ E, GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream E ∧ Set.Infinite E ∧ E ⊆ K

name: GenLimit.Generic.injectiveValueContaminatedPresentationAtMost_mono
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α} {i j : ℕ},
  i ≤ j →
    GenLimit.Generic.InjectiveValueContaminatedPresentationAtMost stream L i →
      GenLimit.Generic.InjectiveValueContaminatedPresentationAtMost stream L j

name: GenLimit.Generic.mem_language_of_mem_sample_of_presents
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream L → ∀ {t : ℕ} {x : α}, x ∈ GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t → x ∈ L

name: GenLimit.Generic.mem_sample_iff
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {t : ℕ} {x : α},
  x ∈ GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t ↔ ∃ s < t, stream s = x

name: GenLimit.Generic.mem_sequenceSample_iff
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {t : ℕ} {xs : Fin t → α} {x : α}, x ∈ GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample xs ↔ ∃ i, xs i = x

name: GenLimit.Generic.mem_versionSpace_iff
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α} {S : Finset α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  L ∈ GenLimit.Generic.versionSpace H S ↔ L ∈ H ∧ ↑S ⊆ L

name: GenLimit.Generic.nonuniform_implies_limit
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α},
  GenLimit.Generic.UUS H → GenLimit.Generic.NonuniformlyGeneratable H → GenLimit.Generic.GeneratableInLimit H

name: GenLimit.Generic.occurrenceContaminatedPresentationAtMost_mono
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α} {i j : ℕ},
  i ≤ j →
    GenLimit.Generic.OccurrenceContaminatedPresentationAtMost stream L i →
      GenLimit.Generic.OccurrenceContaminatedPresentationAtMost stream L j

docstring: Run `G` on the prefix of `stream` strictly before time `t`.
name: GenLimit.Generic.output
type: {α : Type u_1} → GenLimit.Generic.Generator α → GenLimit.Generic.Stream α → ℕ → α

docstring: Number of elements of a finite sample violating `Acceptable`.
name: GenLimit.Generic.rejectedCount
type: {α : Type u_1} → (α → Prop) → Finset α → ℕ

name: GenLimit.Generic.rejectedCount_anti
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {P Q : α → Prop},
  (∀ (x : α), P x → Q x) →
    ∀ (sample : Finset α), GenLimit.Generic.rejectedCount Q sample ≤ GenLimit.Generic.rejectedCount P sample

name: GenLimit.Generic.rejectedCount_le
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (Acceptable : α → Prop) (sample : Finset α),
  GenLimit.Generic.rejectedCount Acceptable sample ≤ sample.card

docstring: Rejected fraction of a finite sample.  Empty samples receive value zero.
name: GenLimit.Generic.rejectedFraction
type: {α : Type u_1} → (α → Prop) → Finset α → ℝ

name: GenLimit.Generic.rejectedFraction_anti
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {P Q : α → Prop},
  (∀ (x : α), P x → Q x) →
    ∀ (sample : Finset α), GenLimit.Generic.rejectedFraction Q sample ≤ GenLimit.Generic.rejectedFraction P sample

name: GenLimit.Generic.rejectedFraction_empty
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (Acceptable : α → Prop), GenLimit.Generic.rejectedFraction Acceptable ∅ = 0

name: GenLimit.Generic.rejectedFraction_le_one
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (Acceptable : α → Prop) (sample : Finset α), GenLimit.Generic.rejectedFraction Acceptable sample ≤ 1

name: GenLimit.Generic.rejectedFraction_nonneg
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (Acceptable : α → Prop) (sample : Finset α), 0 ≤ GenLimit.Generic.rejectedFraction Acceptable sample

docstring: The distinct observations strictly before time `t`.
name: GenLimit.Generic.sample
type: {α : Type u_1} → GenLimit.Generic.Stream α → ℕ → Finset α

name: GenLimit.Generic.sample_card_le
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α) (t : ℕ), (GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t).card ≤ t

docstring:
An injective stream has exactly `t` distinct observations before round
`t`.
name: GenLimit.Generic.sample_card_of_injective
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α),
  Function.Injective stream → ∀ (t : ℕ), (GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t).card = t

name: GenLimit.Generic.sample_card_step
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α) (t : ℕ),
  (GenLimit.Generic.sample stream (t + 1)).card ≤ (GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t).card + 1

docstring: Samples depend only on the corresponding finite stream prefix.
name: GenLimit.Generic.sample_eq_of_eq_on_prefix
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream₁ stream₂ : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {t : ℕ},
  (∀ n < t, stream₁ n = stream₂ n) → GenLimit.Generic.sample stream₁ t = GenLimit.Generic.sample stream₂ t

docstring:
Sampling a finite-history stream at the end of the history recovers
exactly the history's distinct values.
name: GenLimit.Generic.sample_historyThenFallback_length
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] (history : List α) (fallback : α),
  GenLimit.Generic.sample (GenLimit.Generic.historyThenFallback history fallback) history.length = history.toFinset

name: GenLimit.Generic.sample_mono
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {s t : ℕ},
  s ≤ t → GenLimit.Generic.sample stream s ⊆ GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t

name: GenLimit.Generic.sample_subset_commonCore
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α} {S : Finset α}, ↑S ⊆ GenLimit.Generic.commonCore H S

name: GenLimit.Generic.sample_subset_of_streamIn
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  GenLimit.Generic.StreamIn stream L → ∀ (t : ℕ), ↑(GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t) ⊆ L

docstring: The distinct values in a finite sequence.
name: GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample
type: {α : Type u_1} → {t : ℕ} → (Fin t → α) → Finset α

docstring:
An injective finite history has as many distinct observations as
positions.
name: GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample_card_of_injective
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {t : ℕ} (xs : Fin t → α), Function.Injective xs → (GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample xs).card = t

docstring:
Enumerating a finset through its canonical equivalence with `Fin`
recovers exactly that finset as the distinct sample.
name: GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample_equivFin_symm
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (S : Finset α), (GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample fun i => ↑(S.equivFin.symm i)) = S

Passing a list through its canonical `Fin`-indexed input recovers its
underlying finite set of values.
name: GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample_list_get
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] (xs : List α), GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample xs.get = xs.toFinset

name: GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample_prefix
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α) (t : ℕ),
  (GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample fun i => stream ↑i) = GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t

docstring:
Pointwise membership of a finite history implies membership of every
element in its underlying sample.
name: GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample_subset_of_pointwise
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {t : ℕ} {xs : Fin t → α} {S : Set α},
  (∀ (k : Fin t), xs k ∈ S) → ↑(GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample xs) ⊆ S

name: GenLimit.Generic.setDifferenceAtMost_iff_finite_ncard_le
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (A B : Set α) (n : ℕ), GenLimit.Generic.SetDifferenceAtMost A B n ↔ (A \ B).Finite ∧ (A \ B).ncard ≤ n

name: GenLimit.Generic.setDifferenceAtMost_mono
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {A B : Set α} {i j : ℕ},

name: GenLimit.Generic.setDifferenceAtMost_zero_iff_subset
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (A B : Set α), GenLimit.Generic.SetDifferenceAtMost A B 0 ↔ A ⊆ B

Set-valued generation always implies ordinary element-valued generation.
This is the easy direction of P27 Theorem 3.9, stated in the generic Core API.
name: GenLimit.Generic.setGeneratableInLimit_implies_generatableInLimit
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α},
  GenLimit.Generic.SetGeneratableInLimit H → GenLimit.Generic.GeneratableInLimit H

docstring: Run a set-valued generator on the prefix strictly before time `t`.
name: GenLimit.Generic.setOutput
type: {α : Type u_1} → GenLimit.Generic.SetGenerator α → GenLimit.Generic.Stream α → ℕ → Set α

docstring:
A learner that eventually stabilizes to an index denoting each presented
target induces generation in the limit for the extensional range of the
indexed family. No computability assumption is imposed.
name: GenLimit.Generic.stabilizingIndexIdentifier_implies_generatableInLimit
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (F : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageFamily α),
  (∀ (i : ℕ), Set.Infinite (F i)) →
    ∀ (M : GenLimit.Learner α ℕ),
      (∀ (z : ℕ) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α),
          GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream (F z) → GenLimit.IdentifiesInLimit F M stream (F z)) →
        GenLimit.Generic.GeneratableInLimit (Set.range F)

docstring:
A finite history followed by a fallback stays in a language when both
the history and fallback do.
name: GenLimit.Generic.streamIn_historyThenFallback
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {history : List α} {fallback : α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  (∀ x ∈ history, x ∈ L) →
    fallback ∈ L → GenLimit.Generic.StreamIn (GenLimit.Generic.historyThenFallback history fallback) L

name: GenLimit.Generic.streamIn_of_presents
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream L → GenLimit.Generic.StreamIn stream L

name: GenLimit.Generic.target_mem_versionSpace
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  L ∈ H →
    ∀ {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α},
      GenLimit.Generic.StreamIn stream L →
        ∀ (t : ℕ), L ∈ GenLimit.Generic.versionSpace H (GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t)

name: GenLimit.Generic.uniform_implies_limit
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α},
  GenLimit.Generic.UUS H → GenLimit.Generic.UniformlyGeneratable H → GenLimit.Generic.GeneratableInLimit H

name: GenLimit.Generic.uniform_implies_nonuniform
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α},
  GenLimit.Generic.UniformlyGeneratable H → GenLimit.Generic.NonuniformlyGeneratable H

name: GenLimit.Generic.value_mem_sample
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {s t : ℕ}, s < t → stream s ∈ GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t

docstring:
For an injective stream, counting distinct invalid values is equivalent
to counting invalid occurrences.
name: GenLimit.Generic.valuesOutsideAtMost_iff_violationsAtMost_of_injective
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α},
  Function.Injective stream →
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      GenLimit.Generic.ValuesOutsideAtMost stream L n ↔ GenLimit.Generic.ViolationsAtMost stream (fun x => x ∈ L) n

name: GenLimit.Generic.valuesOutsideAtMost_mono
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α} {L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α} {i j : ℕ},
  i ≤ j → GenLimit.Generic.ValuesOutsideAtMost stream L i → GenLimit.Generic.ValuesOutsideAtMost stream L j

name: GenLimit.Generic.valuesOutside_eq_image_violationIndices
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α) (L : GenLimit.Generic.Language α),
  Set.range stream \ L = stream '' GenLimit.Generic.ViolationIndices stream fun x => x ∈ L

docstring: Languages in `H` that contain the positive sample `S`.
name: GenLimit.Generic.versionSpace
type: {α : Type u_1} → GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α → Finset α → Set (GenLimit.Generic.Language α)

Finset-witness form of the occurrence bound, matching papers that write
the finite indicator sum explicitly.

type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} (stream : ℕ → α) (Acceptable : α → Prop) (n : ℕ),
  GenLimit.Generic.ViolationsAtMost stream Acceptable n ↔ ∃ F, F.card ≤ n ∧ ∀ (t : ℕ), t ∈ F ↔ ¬Acceptable (stream t)

name: GenLimit.Generic.violationsAtMost_mono
type:
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {stream : ℕ → α} {Acceptable : α → Prop} {i j : ℕ},
  i ≤ j → GenLimit.Generic.ViolationsAtMost stream Acceptable i → GenLimit.Generic.ViolationsAtMost stream Acceptable j

docstring: The allowable information sequences for each object.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable
type: Type uInfo → Type uObject → Type (max uObject uInfo)

docstring:
Gold's collapsing-uncertainty condition.

Along every allowable sequence for `target`, each different object is
eventually absent from the set of objects compatible with the observed
prefix.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.CollapsingUncertainty
type: {Info : Type u_1} → {Object : Type u_2} → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object → Prop

docstring:
A finite history is compatible with an object when some allowable
information sequence for that object has exactly this prefix.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Compatible
type: {Info : Type u_1} → {Object : Type u_2} → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object → List Info → Object → Prop

docstring:
Gold's distinguishability condition: no allowable information sequence
describes two different objects.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Distinguishable
type: {Info : Type u_1} → {Object : Type u_2} → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object → Prop

docstring: Existence of a possibly noncomputable identifier.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Identifiable
type:
{Name : Type u_1} →
  {Object : Type u_2} →
    {Info : Type u_3} → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming Name Object → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object → Prop

docstring:
A learner identifies every object on each of its allowable information
sequences.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Identifies
type:
{Name : Type u_1} →
  {Object : Type u_2} →
    {Info : Type u_3} →
      GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming Name Object →
        GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object → GenLimit.Learner Info Name → Prop

docstring: Identification on one fixed information sequence.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.IdentifiesOn
type:
{Name : Type u_1} →
  {Object : Type u_2} →
    {Info : Type u_3} →
      GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming Name Object → GenLimit.Learner Info Name → (ℕ → Info) → Object → Prop

docstring:
A naming relation together with a chosen name for every object.

Gold assumes in Theorem 7.1 that every object has at least one name.  Choosing
one such name is harmless in the ineffective layer and is exactly what the
enumeration learner needs in order to issue a conjecture.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming
type: Type uName → Type uObject → Type (max uName uObject)

name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming.denotes
type: {Name : Type uName} → {Object : Type uObject} → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming Name Object → Name → Object

name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming.denotes_nameOf
type:
∀ {Name : Type uName} {Object : Type uObject} (self : GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming Name Object) (object : Object),
  self.denotes (self.nameOf object) = object

name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming.mk
type:
{Name : Type uName} →
  {Object : Type uObject} →
    (denotes : Name → Object) →
      (nameOf : Object → Name) →
        (∀ (object : Object), denotes (nameOf object) = object) → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming Name Object

name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming.nameOf
type: {Name : Type uName} → {Object : Type uObject} → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming Name Object → Object → Name

docstring: The set of all information sequences allowable for at least one object.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.allowableSequences
type: {Info : Type u_1} → {Object : Type u_2} → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object → Set (ℕ → Info)

docstring:
A countable object class with countably many allowable sequences per
object has only countably many allowable sequences in total.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.allowableSequences_countable
type:
∀ {Object : Type u_1} {Info : Type u_2} [Countable Object] {allowable : GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object},
  (∀ (object : Object), (allowable object).Countable) → (GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.allowableSequences allowable).Countable

name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.allowableSequences_eq_iUnion
type:
∀ {Info : Type u_1} {Object : Type u_2} (allowable : GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object),
  GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.allowableSequences allowable = ⋃ object, allowable object

docstring:
Restrict exact positive texts to a specified class of target languages.
Objects outside the class have no allowable information sequences.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.classTextAllowable
type: Set GenLimit.Language → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable ℕ GenLimit.Language

docstring:
Collapsing uncertainty is sufficient for ineffective identification
whenever an enumeration of the object class is supplied.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.collapsingUncertainty_implies_identifiable
type:
∀ {Name : Type u_1} {Object : Type u_2} {Info : Type u_3} (naming : GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming Name Object)
  {allowable : GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object},
  GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.CollapsingUncertainty allowable →
    ∀ (enumeration : ℕ → Object), Function.Surjective enumeration → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Identifiable naming allowable

docstring: Every prefix of an allowable sequence is compatible with its object.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.compatible_textPrefix
type:
∀ {Info : Type u_1} {Object : Type u_2} {allowable : GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object} {object : Object}
  {stream : ℕ → Info},
  stream ∈ allowable object →
    ∀ (t : ℕ), GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Compatible allowable (GenLimit.textPrefix stream t) object

docstring:
Third clause of Gold's Theorem 7.1: for countable information and object
types, if each object has only countably many allowable information
sequences, distinguishability is sufficient for ineffective identification
in the limit.

docstring:
The least compatible enumeration index eventually becomes the first
index naming the target object.  This is the core of the second clause of
Gold's Theorem 7.1.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.firstCompatibleIndex_stabilizes
type:
∀ {Info : Type u_1} {Object : Type u_2} {allowable : GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object},
  GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.CollapsingUncertainty allowable →
    ∀ (enumeration : ℕ → Object) (henumeration : Function.Surjective enumeration) {target : Object} {stream : ℕ → Info},
      stream ∈ allowable target →
        GenLimit.StabilizesTo
          (fun t => GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.firstCompatibleIndex allowable enumeration (GenLimit.textPrefix stream t))
          (GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.firstEnumerationIndex enumeration henumeration target)

docstring:
Exact bundled form of Gold's Theorem 7.1.

The middle conjunct says that *every* surjective enumeration yields a
successful identification-by-enumeration learner.
name: GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.gold_theorem_7_1
type:
∀ {Info : Type u_1} {Object : Type u_2} {Name : Type u_3} [Countable Info] [Countable Object] [Nonempty Object]
  (naming : GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Naming Name Object) (allowable : GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Allowable Info Object),
  (∀ (object : Object), (allowable object).Countable) →
    (GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Identifiable naming allowable → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Distinguishable allowable) ∧
      (GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.CollapsingUncertainty allowable →
          ∀ (enumeration : ℕ → Object),
            Function.Surjective enumeration →
              GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Identifies naming allowable
                (GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.identificationByEnumeration naming allowable enumeration)) ∧
        (GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Distinguishable allowable → GenLimit.Gold.Abstract.Identifiable naming allowable)

type:

docstring:
The finite-set learner identifies every finite language from arbitrary
positive text.  This is Gold's Theorem I.6 under `finiteNaming`,
where finite sets serve as names for their underlying languages.
Gold's original theorem uses the tester-naming relation and
also requires an effective compilation from each observed finite set to a
tester program; that compilation is not formalized here.
For the empty language, although
`finiteLanguages` includes the empty language, every total positive text
`stream : ℕ → ℕ` has a nonempty range.  Hence no stream satisfies
`Presents stream ∅`, and the universally quantified identification statement
for `∅` holds vacuously.

GenLimit.Gold.Text.IdentifiesClass GenLimit.Gold.Text.finiteNaming GenLimit.Gold.Text.finiteLearner
  GenLimit.Gold.Text.finiteLanguages

docstring:

language in `𝒞`, then every infinite member of `𝒞` has a finite tell-tale.

its finite content nonempty, avoiding the vacuity of exact stream
presentations for the empty language.

  GenLimit.Gold.Text.SemanticallyIdentifiesClass M 𝒞 → L ∈ 𝒞 → Set.Infinite L → ∃ D, GenLimit.Gold.Text.IsTellTale 𝒞 L D

docstring:
Corollary 6.16: every positive error allowance gives an element
generator with lower density at least `(ρ - ε) / 2`.
name: GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.Results.corollary_6_16
type:
∀ (setGen : GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.SetGenerator ℕ),
  GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.IsInfiniteSetGenerator setGen →
    ∀ (family : ℕ → Set ℕ) (selection : (t : ℕ) → (Fin t → ℕ) → Finset ℕ)
      (orders : ℕ → GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) (ρ ε : ℝ),
      0 < ε →
        GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.SetCoreSelectionInvariant setGen family selection →
          (∀ (i : ℕ), (orders i).carrier = family i) →
            (∀ (i : ℕ), GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankFallback.InheritsAmbientOrder (orders i)) →
              ∀ (target : ℕ) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream ℕ),
                (∃ N, ∀ (t : ℕ), N ≤ t → target ∈ selection t fun i => stream ↑i) →
                  ρ ≤ GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.setBasedLowerDensity setGen (orders target) stream →
                    ∃ gen,
                      GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.GeneratesElementInLimitOn gen (family target) stream ∧
                        (ρ - ε) / 2 ≤ GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.elementBasedLowerDensity gen (orders target) stream

docstring:
Lemma 7.5: bounded displacement transfers empirical lower and upper
density to canonical ordered density.
name: GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.Results.lemma_7_5
type:
∀ (K : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream ℕ),
  ∀ L ⊆ K.carrier,
    ∀ (M : ℝ),
      0 < M →
        GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.BoundedDisplacement K stream K.carrier M →
          1 / M * Filter.liminf (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.empiricalTargetRatio stream L) Filter.atTop ≤
              K.lowerDensity L ∧
            1 / M * Filter.limsup (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.empiricalTargetRatio stream L) Filter.atTop ≤
              K.upperDensity L

docstring:
Theorem 6.1: Algorithm 5 generates under finite noise and attains
set-based upper density at least `1 - c` under `c`-omissions.
name: GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.Results.theorem_6_1
type:
∀ (O : GenLimit.OracleFamily) (orders : ℕ → GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage),

        GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.FiniteNoise stream (O.language z) →
          GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.OmissionsAtMost stream (orders z) c →

                (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmFiveGenerator
                  (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.finiteExpansionOracleFamily O).language)

              1 - c ≤
                GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.setBasedUpperDensity
                  (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmFiveGenerator
                    (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.finiteExpansionOracleFamily O).language)

docstring:
Theorem 6.15: Algorithm 8 converts an eventually `ρ`-dense set
generator into a fresh element generator of lower density at least `ρ / 2`.
The ambient-order compatibility implicit in the paper is explicit here.
name: GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.Results.theorem_6_15
type:
∀ (setGen : GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.SetGenerator ℕ)
  (hinfinite : GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.IsInfiniteSetGenerator setGen) (family : ℕ → Set ℕ)
  (selection : (t : ℕ) → (Fin t → ℕ) → Finset ℕ) (orders : ℕ → GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) (ρ : ℝ),
  0 < ρ →
    GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.SetCoreSelectionInvariant setGen family selection →
      (∀ (i : ℕ), (orders i).carrier = family i) →
        (∀ (i : ℕ), GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankFallback.InheritsAmbientOrder (orders i)) →
          ∀ (target : ℕ) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream ℕ),
            (∃ N, ∀ (t : ℕ), N ≤ t → target ∈ selection t fun i => stream ↑i) →
              (∃ N,
                  ∀ (t : ℕ),
                    N ≤ t →
                      ρ ≤ (orders target).lowerDensity (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.setOutput setGen stream t)) →
                GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.GeneratesElementInLimitOn
                    (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmEightGenerator setGen hinfinite selection orders ρ)
                    (family target) stream ∧
                  ρ / 2 ≤
                    GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.elementBasedLowerDensity
                      (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmEightGenerator setGen hinfinite selection orders ρ)
                      (orders target) stream

docstring:
Theorem 6.18: finite-expansion compilation preserves lower and upper
element-density guarantees under the paper's common ambient ordering.
name: GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.Results.theorem_6_18
type:
∀ (O : GenLimit.OracleFamily) (orders expansionOrders : ℕ → GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage),
  (∀ (i : ℕ), (orders i).carrier = O.language i) →
    (∀ (j : ℕ),
        (expansionOrders j).carrier = (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.finiteExpansionOracleFamily O).language j) →
      (∀ (j : ℕ) (A : GenLimit.Language),
          (expansionOrders j).lowerDensity A =
              (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.finiteExpansionMeasure orders j).lowerDensity A ∧
            (expansionOrders j).upperDensity A =
              (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.finiteExpansionMeasure orders j).upperDensity A) →
        ∀ (gen : GenLimit.Generic.Generator ℕ) (ρlow ρup : ℝ),
          (∀ (j : ℕ) (stream : ℕ → ℕ),
              GenLimit.Presents stream ((GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.finiteExpansionOracleFamily O).language j) →
                GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.GeneratesElementInLimitOn gen
                    ((GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.finiteExpansionOracleFamily O).language j) stream ∧
                  GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.ElementDensityGuaranteeOn gen (expansionOrders j) stream ρlow ρup) →
            ∀ (z : ℕ) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream ℕ),
              GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.FiniteNoiseFiniteOmissionEnumeration stream (O.language z) →
                GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.GeneratesElementInLimitOn gen (O.language z) stream ∧
                  GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.ElementDensityGuaranteeOn gen (orders z) stream ρlow ρup

docstring:

type:
∀ (c : ℝ) (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (ε : ℝ),

      ¬GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.GuaranteesSetBasedUpperDensityUnderOmissionsOn gen
          (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.theoremSixFourFamily (1 - c))
          (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.theoremSixFourOrders (1 - c) ⋯ ⋯) c (1 - c + ε)

docstring:
Theorem 6.5: set-based lower-density generation under finite noise and
finite omissions is equivalent to the pairwise finite-difference density
condition.
name: GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.Results.theorem_6_5
type:
∀ (O : GenLimit.OracleFamily) (orders : ℕ → GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage),
  (∀ (i : ℕ), (orders i).carrier = O.language i) →
    ∀ (c : ℝ),
      (∃ gen,
          GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.IsInfiniteSetGenerator gen ∧
            ∀ (z : ℕ),
              GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.GeneratesSetUnderFiniteContaminationOn gen (orders z).carrier ∧
                GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.GuaranteesSetBasedLowerDensityUnderFiniteContaminationOn gen (orders z)
                  c) ↔
        ∀ (i j : ℕ), Set.Finite (O.language i \ O.language j) → c ≤ (orders j).lowerDensity (O.language i)

docstring:
Theorem 7.8: Algorithm 9 generates under vanishing noise and
`M`-bounded displacement with eventual set-based lower density
`(1 - ε) / M`.
name: GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.Results.theorem_7_8
type:
∀ (family : ℕ → Set ℕ),
  (∀ (i : ℕ), (family i).Infinite) →
    ∀ (orders : ℕ → GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage),
      (∀ (i : ℕ), (orders i).carrier = family i) →
        ∀ (ε M : ℝ),
          0 < ε →
            ε < 1 →
              0 < M →
                ∀ (target : ℕ) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream ℕ),
                  Function.Injective stream →
                    GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.VanishingNoise stream (family target) →
                      GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.BoundedDisplacement (orders target) stream (orders target).carrier
                          M →
                        GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.GeneratesInfiniteSetInLimitOn
                            (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmNineSetGenerator family orders ε M) (family target)
                            stream ∧
                          ∃ T,
                            ∀ (t : ℕ),
                              T ≤ t →
                                (1 - ε) / M ≤
                                  (orders target).lowerDensity
                                    (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.setOutput
                                      (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmNineSetGenerator family orders ε M)
                                      stream t)

    ∀ {t m : ℕ} (xs : Fin t → ℕ),
      GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmEightChosenSet setGen selection orders ρ xs ⊆ K.carrier →
        2 * t < K.prefixCount (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmEightChosenSet setGen selection orders ρ xs) m →
          GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.canonicalRank K K.carrier
              (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmEightOutput setGen hinfinite selection orders ρ t xs) ≤
            m

name: GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmEightOutput_spec
type:
∀ (setGen : GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.SetGenerator ℕ)
  (hinfinite : GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.IsInfiniteSetGenerator setGen)
  (selection : (t : ℕ) → (Fin t → ℕ) → Finset ℕ) (orders : ℕ → GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) (ρ : ℝ) {t : ℕ}
  (xs : Fin t → ℕ),
  have output := GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmEightOutput setGen hinfinite selection orders ρ t xs;
  output ∈ GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmEightChosenSet setGen selection orders ρ xs ∧
    output ∉ GenLimit.Generic.sequenceSample xs ∧
      ∀ (s : Fin t),
        output ≠
          GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmEightOutput setGen hinfinite selection orders ρ ↑s fun j => xs ⟨↑j, ⋯⟩

    GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.SetCoreSelectionInvariant setGen family selection →

docstring:
Definition 3's global element-generator condition for the concrete
Algorithm 4: on every stream and at every round, the output avoids both the
entire observed prefix and all earlier outputs.

The source requires this before its separate eventual target-validity
condition.  It holds at every round, not merely after priority stabilization:
the empty ranked prefix has common core `univ`, which is infinite because the
paper assumes every language (in particular `family 0`) is infinite.

  (∀ (i : ℕ), Set.Infinite (family i)) →
    ∀ (threshold : ℕ → ℝ) (fallback : α) (stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream α) (t : ℕ),
      GenLimit.Generic.output (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmFourGenerator family threshold fallback) stream
            t ∉
          GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t ∧
        GenLimit.Generic.output (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmFourGenerator family threshold fallback) stream
            t ∉
          GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.generatedBefore
            (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmFourGenerator family threshold fallback) stream t

At time `t`, the rule chooses from the maximal infinite prefix core while
avoiding both the observed finite history and every output produced on a
strict prefix of that same history.  The fallback branch makes the definition
total for arbitrary families.  For the paper's families of infinite
languages, `algorithmFourGenerator_fresh_every_round` below shows that the
selected core is infinite and the fallback is never used at any round.

      (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.finiteCommonCore
        (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.indexedLanguages family
          (GenLimit.InfiniteContamination.algorithmFourHistoryIndices family threshold fallback xs))) →

    output ∈
