type:
∀ {C : GenLimit.LanguageFamily} {Edge : Type u_1}
  (spec : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.RunSpec C Edge)
  (round : ℕ) {edge : Edge},
  edge ∈ spec.edgesAt round →
    ∃ first second,
      { tag := GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.firstTag round edge,
            value := first } ∈
          (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.stateAt spec
              (round + 1)).ledger ∧
        { tag := GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.secondTag round edge,
              value := second } ∈
            (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.stateAt spec
                (round + 1)).ledger ∧
          first ≠ second ∧
            GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.outputAt spec
                  round ≤
                first ∧
              GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.outputAt spec
                  round ≤
                second

docstring:
Historical queue priority for the recursive run.  If a reserved value has
not yet appeared in the exact input/output history and is not the current
input, then the current emitted value is no larger in ambient `ℕ` order.

This is the operational analogue of `Schedule.priority_available`; converting
it to that field still requires a target-language position comparison.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.output_le_reserved_value_ambient
type:
∀ {C : GenLimit.LanguageFamily} {Edge : Type u_1}
  (spec : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.RunSpec C Edge)
  {reservationRound currentRound token : ℕ},
  reservationRound ≤ currentRound →
    ∀ {reservation : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.Reservation Edge},
      reservation ∈
          (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.reservedAt spec
              reservationRound).ledger →
        reservation.value = token →
          ¬GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.UsedBefore spec.input
                (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.outputAt
                  spec)
                currentRound token →
            token ≠ spec.input currentRound →
              GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.outputAt spec
                  currentRound ≤
                token

docstring:

at every later round while that token remains unused.

type:

  (side : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.ReservationSide) {round : ℕ},
  (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.runTokenSource spec).round
        d ≤
      round →
    ¬GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.UsedBefore spec.input
          (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.outputAt spec)
          round
          ((GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.runTokenSource
                spec).token
            d side) →
      (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.runTokenSource
                spec).token
            d side ≠
          spec.input round →
        GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.outputAt spec round ≤
          (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.RecursiveHistory.runTokenSource
                spec).token
            d side

          (edges : List Edge) →
            GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.SequentiallyFresh state.ledger
                (insert input state.used) round language hInfinite edges →

docstring:
The concrete allocation-then-emission transition discharges queue
priority for both tokens of every newly reserved edge.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.reserveBatchForInput_pair_priority
type:
∀ {C : GenLimit.LanguageFamily} {Edge : Type u_1} (hFamilyInfinite : ∀ (n : ℕ), Set.Infinite (C n))
  (state : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.TaggedOutputState Edge)
  (input round : ℕ) (current : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.FamilyPoint C)
  (language : Edge → GenLimit.Language) (hInfinite : ∀ (edge : Edge), Set.Infinite (language edge)) (edges : List Edge)
  (hFresh :
    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.SequentiallyFresh state.ledger
      (insert input state.used) round language hInfinite edges)
  {edge : Edge},
  edge ∈ edges →
    have reserved :=
      GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.reserveBatchForInput state input round
        language hInfinite edges hFresh;
    ∃ first second,
      { tag := GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.firstTag round edge,
            value := first } ∈
          reserved.ledger ∧
        { tag := GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.secondTag round edge,
              value := second } ∈
            reserved.ledger ∧
          first ≠ second ∧
            GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.taggedEmission hFamilyInfinite
                  reserved input current ≤
                first ∧
              GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.taggedEmission hFamilyInfinite
                  reserved input current ≤
                second

docstring:
The pair records and their same-round priority inequalities survive into
the post-output ledger, exactly the snapshot used by a historical family.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.reserveBatchThenOutput_pair
type:
∀ {C : GenLimit.LanguageFamily} {Edge : Type u_1} (hFamilyInfinite : ∀ (n : ℕ), Set.Infinite (C n))
  (state : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.TaggedOutputState Edge)
  (input round : ℕ) (current : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.FamilyPoint C)
  (language : Edge → GenLimit.Language) (hInfinite : ∀ (edge : Edge), Set.Infinite (language edge)) (edges : List Edge)
  (hFresh :
    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.SequentiallyFresh state.ledger
      (insert input state.used) round language hInfinite edges)
  {edge : Edge},
  edge ∈ edges →
    ∃ first second,
      { tag := GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.firstTag round edge,
            value := first } ∈
          (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.reserveBatchThenOutput
              hFamilyInfinite state input round current language hInfinite edges hFresh).ledger ∧
        { tag := GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.secondTag round edge,
              value := second } ∈
            (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.reserveBatchThenOutput
                hFamilyInfinite state input round current language hInfinite edges hFresh).ledger ∧
          first ≠ second ∧
            GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.taggedEmission hFamilyInfinite
                  (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.reserveBatchForInput state
                    input round language hInfinite edges hFresh)
                  input current ≤
                first ∧
              GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.taggedEmission hFamilyInfinite
                  (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.FirstConsumptionBridge.reserveBatchForInput state
                    input round language hInfinite edges hFresh)
                  input current ≤
                second

type:
{K : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage} →
  {Output Long : GenLimit.Language} →
    (retained : Set ℕ) →
      (charge : ℕ → ℕ) →
        (inputFirst : ℕ → Prop) →
          (longError : ℕ) →
            (∀ ⦃i : ℕ⦄, i ∈ retained → K.enumeration i ∈ Long) →
              (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
                  K.prefixCount Long n ≤
                    2 * GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.positionPrefixCount retained n + longError) →
                (∀ ⦃i : ℕ⦄, i ∈ retained → charge i < i) →
                  (∀ ⦃i : ℕ⦄, i ∈ retained → K.enumeration (charge i) ∈ Output) →
                    Set.InjOn charge (retained ∩ {i | inputFirst i}) →
                      Set.InjOn charge (retained ∩ {i | ¬inputFirst i}) →
                        GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.LongBadCapacityTwoCharge K Output Long

          (charge : ℕ → ℕ) →

                (∀ ⦃i : ℕ⦄, i ∈ retained \ ↑exceptions → K.enumeration (charge i) ∈ Output) →
                  Set.InjOn charge (retained \ ↑exceptions ∩ {i | inputFirst i}) →
                    Set.InjOn charge (retained \ ↑exceptions ∩ {i | ¬inputFirst i}) →
                      GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.LongBadCapacityTwoCharge K Output Long

type:

docstring:

round-and-edge label is one of the two witnessed side records.  Together with
their distinct values, this rules out both missing and extra physical
reservations for the event.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.HasPairProvenance.exactTwo
type:
∀ {Edge : Type u_1} {ledger : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.Ledger Edge}
  {round : ℕ} {edge : Edge},
  GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.Valid ledger →
    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.HasPairProvenance ledger round edge →
      ∃ first second,
        { tag := GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.firstTag round edge,
              value := first } ∈
            ledger ∧
          { tag := GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.secondTag round edge,
                value := second } ∈
              ledger ∧
            first ≠ second ∧
              ∀ reservation ∈ ledger,
                reservation.tag.round = round →
                  reservation.tag.edge = edge →
                    reservation =
                        {
                          tag :=
                            GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.firstTag round edge,
                          value := first } ∨
                      reservation =
                        {
                          tag :=
                            GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.secondTag round edge,
                          value := second }

      ∃ first second,
        { tag := GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.firstTag round edge,
              value := first } ∈
            ledger ∧
          { tag := GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.secondTag round edge,
                value := second } ∈
              ledger ∧
            first ≠ second ∧
              (∀ reservation ∈ ledger,
                  reservation.tag =
                      GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.firstTag round edge →
                    reservation =
                      { tag := GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.firstTag round edge,
                        value := first }) ∧
                ∀ reservation ∈ ledger,
                  reservation.tag =
                      GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ReservationLedger.secondTag round edge →
                    reservation =

docstring:
A structural certificate for thinning arbitrary non-singleton ordered
runs.

Every omitted point has an adjacent retained mate, and different omissions
have different mates.  Deleting one point from each disjoint non-singleton
consecutive run yields precisely this local accounting obligation.

        (∀ ⦃i : ℕ⦄, i ∈ P → i ∉ retained → mate i + 1 = i ∨ i + 1 = mate i) →
          Set.InjOn mate (P \ retained) →
            GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.RunThinning.Certificate P retained

docstring:
A backward two-token charge certificate.

The two reservations of each retained position are globally distinct.
Every reservation is consumed either by a generator output or by an
adversary input; in the latter case `hit` is the output paired with that input
round.  The two classwise injectivity fields state exactly that an output can
be charged at most once in each way.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TwoTokenCharge
type: Set ℕ → Set ℕ → Type u_1 → Type u_1

name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TwoTokenCharge.consumption

{retained output : Set ℕ} →
  {Token : Type u_1} →
    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TwoTokenCharge retained output Token →
      Token → GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TokenConsumption

type:
{retained output : Set ℕ} →
  {Token : Type u_1} →
    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TwoTokenCharge retained output Token → Token → ℕ

name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TwoTokenCharge.hit_earlier
GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TwoTokenCharge.hit_output
GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TwoTokenCharge.input_hit_injective
type:
∀ {retained output : Set ℕ} {Token : Type u_1}
  (self : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TwoTokenCharge retained output Token),
  Set.InjOn self.hit
    (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ownedTokens retained self.token ∩
      {x | self.consumption x = GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TokenConsumption.input})

name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TwoTokenCharge.mk
type:
{retained output : Set ℕ} →
  {Token : Type u_1} →
    (token : ℕ → Bool → Token) →
      (∀ ⦃i j : ℕ⦄,
          i ∈ retained → j ∈ retained → ∀ ⦃side side' : Bool⦄, token i side = token j side' → i = j ∧ side = side') →
        (consumption : Token → GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TokenConsumption) →
          (hit : Token → ℕ) →
            (∀ ⦃i : ℕ⦄, i ∈ retained → ∀ (side : Bool), hit (token i side) ∈ output) →
              (∀ ⦃i : ℕ⦄, i ∈ retained → ∀ (side : Bool), hit (token i side) < i) →
                Set.InjOn hit
                    (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ownedTokens retained token ∩
                      {x |
                        consumption x = GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TokenConsumption.output}) →
                  Set.InjOn hit
                      (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.ownedTokens retained token ∩
                        {x |
                          consumption x = GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TokenConsumption.input}) →
                    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TwoTokenCharge retained output Token

docstring:
An injective charge into output positions gives the second cardinal
inequality used for retained positions of long bad runs.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.card_le_of_injective_charge
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] (source : Finset α) (target : Finset β)
  (charge : α → β), Set.MapsTo charge ↑source ↑target → Set.InjOn charge ↑source → source.card ≤ target.card

docstring:
Pure finite counting core.

Each source element owns two slots.  Every slot hits the target, and the hit
map is injective separately on output-consumed and input-consumed slots.
Consequently a target can be hit at most twice, once from each class.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.card_le_of_two_token_consumption
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] (source : Finset α) (target : Finset β)
  (consumption : α × Bool → GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TokenConsumption) (hit : α × Bool → β),
  (∀ p ∈ GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.twoTokenPairs source, hit p ∈ target) →
    Set.InjOn hit
        ↑({p ∈ GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.twoTokenPairs source |
            consumption p = GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TokenConsumption.output}) →
      Set.InjOn hit
          ↑({p ∈ GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.twoTokenPairs source |
              consumption p = GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.TokenConsumption.input}) →
        source.card ≤ target.card

docstring:
A map with fibers of size at most two gives the cardinal inequality used
for the paper's good-missing-string charge.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.card_le_two_mul_of_fibers
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [DecidableEq α] [inst : DecidableEq β] (source : Finset α) (target : Finset β)
  (charge : α → β),
  (∀ x ∈ source, charge x ∈ target) →
    (∀ y ∈ target, {x ∈ source | charge x = y}.card ≤ 2) → source.card ≤ 2 * target.card

docstring:
A generic analytic transfer: an eventual estimate
`n ≤ q * D n + error` forces lower density at least `1/q`.

The upper bound on `D` supplies the boundedness hypothesis required by the
`liminf` comparison theorem.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.InfiniteRank.lowerDensity_inv_of_eventual_counting
type:
∀ (D : ℕ → ℕ) (q error : ℕ),
  0 < q →
    (∀ (n : ℕ), D n ≤ n) →
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, n ≤ q * D n + error) → 1 / ↑q ≤ Filter.liminf (fun n => ↑(D n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop

docstring:
Uniform-counting convenience wrapper for

type:
∀ (D : ℕ → ℕ) (q error : ℕ),
  0 < q →
    (∀ (n : ℕ), D n ≤ n) → (∀ (n : ℕ), n ≤ q * D n + error) → 1 / ↑q ≤ Filter.liminf (fun n => ↑(D n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop

docstring:
Direct ordered-language interface for the dynamic part of Theorem 6.12.

A future implementation needs only instantiate the four prefix counts, prove
their partition identity, and establish the three eventual inequalities.  In

docstring:
The exact finite-prefix accounting lemma behind the constant `1/8`.

The error terms permit removal of a finite initial prefix and the one boundary
position which can arise when a run is cut by the end of a prefix.

type:
∀ (n o g s b eSingleton eGood eLong : ℕ),
  o + g + s + b = n →
    2 * s ≤ o + g + s + eSingleton → g ≤ 2 * o + eGood → b ≤ 2 * o + eLong → n ≤ 8 * o + eSingleton + 2 * eGood + eLong

docstring:

long-bad coefficient from two to four.  The unchanged singleton and good
estimates then give the corrected constant ten.

  o + g + s + b = n →

docstring: Uniform form of `theorem_6_12_one_eighth_of_eventual_counting`.

type:

docstring:
What survives from the failed temporal-persistence intuition at one
fixed round.  If `m` is an eligible parent candidate, the selected path
either reaches its language or reaches a sublanguage already at least as
high in Cantor--Bendixson level.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.PersistenceCounterexample.fixed_round_replacement
type:
∀ {C : GenLimit.LanguageFamily} {stream : ℕ → ℕ} {r round m : ℕ}
  {hr :
    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.TowerTopology.FiniteRankAtMost
      (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.FamilySpace C) r},
  m ≤ round →
    ∀ (child : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.RemainingPoint C stream round),
      GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.StrictCritical C stream (round + 1) m →
        ↑↑child ⊂ C m →
          GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.levelOf hr ↑child <
              GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.levelOf hr
                (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.familyPoint C m) →
            ∃ replacement,
              GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.ProperAncestorAt C stream r hr round child
                  replacement ∧
                ↑↑replacement ⊆ C m ∧
                  (↑↑replacement = C m ∨
                    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.levelOf hr
                        (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.familyPoint C m) ≤
                      GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.levelOf hr ↑replacement)

type:

  m ≤ round →
    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.StrictCritical C stream (round + 1) m →
      ∀ (current : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.RemainingPoint C stream round),
        ↑↑current ⊂ C m →
          GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.levelOf hr ↑current <
              GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.levelOf hr
                (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.familyPoint C m) →

A viable repair for the source's cross-round step: compare the persistent
fallback and the new identified language inside one old forest.  Every common
ancestor then climbs strictly above the fallback whenever the new language
escapes it by inclusion.

type:

  {fallback newGuess common : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.RemainingPoint C stream round},
  GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.AncestorAt C stream r hr round fallback common →
    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.AncestorAt C stream r hr round newGuess common →
      ¬↑↑newGuess ⊆ ↑↑fallback →
        GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.ProperAncestorAt C stream r hr round fallback common ∧
          GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.levelOf hr ↑fallback <

The exact parent forest can lose a still-consistent ancestor even when
the semantic child language is unchanged.  At round zero the only eligible
level-one parent is `topLanguage`.  Revealing `2` purges the finite blocker,
makes `evenLanguage` strictly critical, and the finite maximum-index branch
rewires the child to `evenLanguage`.  Both possible parents have level one,
so `topLanguage` is no longer on the path.

---

Corollary 6.10: after stabilization, every transition on which the
accurate selector changes language chooses a fallback contained in the true
target.  The returned vertices are the canonical selector values in their
respective post-observation forests.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.Results.theorem_6_2_finite_rank_endgame
type:
∀ {C : GenLimit.LanguageFamily} {stream : ℕ → ℕ} {r z : ℕ}
  (hr :
    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.TowerTopology.FiniteRankAtMost
      (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.FamilySpace C) r),
  GenLimit.Presents stream (C z) →
    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FirstOccurrence C z →
      ∃ T,
        ∀ (round : ℕ),
          T ≤ round →
            ∃ current next,
              ↑current = GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.identifiedPointAt C stream round ∧
                ↑next = GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankParent.identifiedPointAt C stream (round + 1) ∧
                  (↑↑current ≠ ↑↑next →
                    ∃ fallback,
                      GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankFallback.fallbackChoice C stream r hr round
                            current next =
                          some fallback ∧
                        ↑fallback ⊆ C z)

docstring:
Shared analytic transfer for ordered lower density.

If, up to an asymptotically vanishing error, every source prefix ratio is at
most `q` times the corresponding output ratio, then the output lower density
is at least the source lower density divided by `q`. Paper-specific files
should prove their finite counting inequality and instantiate this theorem,
rather than duplicating the `liminf` argument.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage.lowerDensity_div_le_of_eventually_prefixRatio_le
type:
∀ (K : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) (source output : GenLimit.Language) (q : ℝ),
  0 < q →
    ∀ (error : ℕ → ℝ),
      Filter.Tendsto error Filter.atTop (nhds 0) →
        (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, K.prefixRatio source n ≤ q * K.prefixRatio output n + error n) →
          K.lowerDensity source / q ≤ K.lowerDensity output

docstring:
A selected incomparable fallback is a common superset of both current
identified sets, and is minimal among all common predecessor positions in
the old chain.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.commonPredecessorGuess_spec
type:
∀ (old new : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.IdentifiedIntersectionState)
  (hOldInfinite : Set.Infinite old.identified)
  (aggressive : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.AggressiveGuess),
  GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.commonPredecessorGuess old new hOldInfinite =
      some aggressive →
    old.identified ⊆ aggressive.language ∧
      new.identified ⊆ aggressive.language ∧
        ∃ (h : (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.commonPredecessorOldIndices old new).Nonempty),
          aggressive.language =
              old.chain (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.commonPredecessorOldIndex old new h) ∧
            aggressive.token =
                2 *
                  (new.chosenIndex -
                    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.commonPredecessorNewIndex old new h) ∧
              ∀ i ∈ GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.commonPredecessorOldIndices old new,
                aggressive.language ⊆ old.chain i

return.  If two later rounds had the same latest return, their identified
sets would agree, making the earlier round a still later return for the

      GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.latestReturn identified cutoff t < t ∧
        identified (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.latestReturn identified cutoff t) =

the post-observation state is the observation round itself.  Thus a theorem
which needs a *strictly pre-observation* return cannot follow from mere prior
return existence.

      GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.latestReturn identified cutoff (t + 1) = t

docstring:
Conditional bad-charge fragment produced by the normalized warm-up run.

`hCovered` is exactly the remaining mathematical obligation: every
nonexceptional bad input must possess the strict pre-observation return
encoded by `LateReturnEligibleRank`.  All output, order, and injectivity
fields then follow from the concrete run.

type:
(C : GenLimit.LanguageFamily) →
  (stream : ℕ → ℕ) →
    (hLanguagesInfinite : ∀ (i : ℕ), Set.Infinite (C i)) →
      (K : GenLimit.KleinbergWei.OrderedLanguage) →
        GenLimit.KleinbergWei.DensityMeasures.FiniteRankFallback.InheritsAmbientOrder K →
          (cutoff : ℕ) →
            (bad : GenLimit.Language) →
              (exceptions : Finset ℕ) →
                (∀ (t : ℕ),
                    cutoff ≤ t →
                      GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.sourceWarmupOutput C stream
                          hLanguagesInfinite t ∈
                        K.carrier) →
                  (∀ (i : ℕ),
                      K.enumeration i ∈ bad →
                        i ∉ exceptions →
                          GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.LateReturnEligibleRank C stream
                            hLanguagesInfinite K cutoff i) →
                    GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.WarmupBadChargeFragment K
                      (Set.range
                        (GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.WarmupPriority.sourceWarmupOutput C stream
                          hLanguagesInfinite))

docstring:
Correct finite arithmetic for the four prefix classes in the pod proof.

Here `insideMissed` and `insideOutput` count the two parts of `C` already in
pods, while `good` and `bad` count the two classes outside all pods.  Each
inside class is bounded by the output count, and `s` copies of either outside
class are charged into the output plus `insideMissed` and an error.  The
source's displayed algebra contains an extra division by `s`; the inequality
below is the dimensionally consistent conclusion.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.fixedPod_finite_counting
type:
∀ (s enumerated output insideMissed insideOutput good bad error : ℕ),
  enumerated ≤ insideMissed + insideOutput + good + bad →
    insideMissed ≤ output →
      insideOutput ≤ output →
        s * good ≤ output + insideMissed + error →
          s * bad ≤ output + insideMissed + error → s * enumerated ≤ (2 * s + 4) * output + 2 * error

docstring:

docstring:
Equations (4)--(6), the finite-stabilization heart of Lemma 2.5 Item 1:
eventually the prefix through the target is fixed, full, valid, and
infinite.
name: GenLimit.KleinbergWei.PartialEnumeration.lemma_2_5_stable_targetPrefix
type:
∀ {C : GenLimit.LanguageFamily} {stream : ℕ → ℕ} {E : GenLimit.Language} {z : ℕ},
  GenLimit.Presents stream E →
    Set.Infinite E →
      E ⊆ C z →
        ∃ T,

docstring: Conditional machine-independent merge-order core for Theorem 21.
name: GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.Results.theorem_21_msm_merge_order_core
type:
∀ {Candidate : Type u_1} {Config : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq Candidate] (candidates : Config → Finset Candidate)
  (score : Config → Candidate → ℕ) (merge : Config → Candidate → Config) (remaining : Config → ℕ)
  (intended : Config → Candidate → Prop) (Sound Complete : Config → Prop) (initial : Config),
  Sound initial →
    (∀ (config : Config),
        Sound config → ¬Complete config → ∃ good ∈ candidates config, intended config good ∧ 2 ≤ score config good) →
      (∀ (config : Config),
          Sound config → ¬Complete config → ∀ bad ∈ candidates config, ¬intended config bad → score config bad ≤ 1) →
        (∀ (config : Config) (choice : Candidate),
            Sound config → intended config choice → Sound (merge config choice)) →
          (∀ (config : Config),
              Sound config → Complete config → GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.IsMSMTerminal candidates score config) →
            (∀ (config : Config) (choice : Candidate),
                GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.IsMSMChoice candidates score config choice →
                  remaining (merge config choice) < remaining config) →
              ∃ final,
                Relation.ReflTransGen (GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.MSMStep candidates score merge) initial final ∧
                  Sound final ∧ Complete final ∧ GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.IsMSMTerminal candidates score final

  (GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.taggedMachine M).toFST.runFrom (Sum.inl q) [Sum.inl a, Sum.inr (q, a)] =
    (Sum.inl (M.step q a).1,
      [GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.markerAction (q, a),
        GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.liftAction (M.step q a).2])

type:

    ∀ (stream : ℕ → Sample) (source : Set Sample),
      GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.Covers stream source →
        (∀ e ∈ used, witness e ∈ source) →
          (GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.transitionCover used witness).card ≤ used.card ∧
            (∀ e ∈ used,
                ∃ sample ∈ GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.transitionCover used witness, e ∈ exercises sample) ∧
              ∃ t, ∀ sample ∈ GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.transitionCover used witness, ∃ n < t, stream n = sample

docstring:
Corollary 18's exact characteristic-set information-order implication.

If a learner using poorer observations has characteristic cores bounded by
an arbitrary core measure, then erasing information gives a
richer-observation learner with the identical bound.  Consequently, any
impossibility for the richer observation model transfers contrapositively
to the poorer one once the source-specific machine impossibility is
available.
name: GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.corollary_18_characteristic_bound_lifts_to_richer_observations
type:
∀ {Input : Type u_1} {Poor : Type u_2} {Rep : Sort u_3} {Model : Sort u_4} {Rich : Type u_5} {Output : Type u_6}
  (learner : Set (Input × Poor) → Rep) (rich : Model → Input → Rich) (forget : Rich → Poor)
  (modelSemantics : Model → Input → Option Output) (representationSemantics : Rep → Input → Option Output)
  (source : Set Input) (mass : Set Input → ℕ) (bound : Model → ℕ),
  (∀ (m : Model),
      ∃ core,
        GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.IsCharacteristicSet learner (fun model input => forget (rich model input))
            modelSemantics representationSemantics source m core ∧
          mass core ≤ bound m) →
    ∀ (m : Model),
      ∃ core,
        GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.IsCharacteristicSet
            (GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.liftLearnerAlongForget learner forget) rich modelSemantics
            representationSemantics source m core ∧
          mass core ≤ bound m

docstring:

(`unintended ≤ 1`, some intended `≥ 2`) forces the greedy maximum to be an
intended merge.

type:

  GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.IsMSMChoice candidates score config choice →
    good ∈ candidates config →
      intended config good →
        2 ≤ score config good →
          (∀ bad ∈ candidates config, ¬intended config bad → score config bad ≤ 1) → intended config choice

docstring:
Soundness is preserved along every finite MSM run when incomplete sound
configurations satisfy separation, complete sound configurations are
terminal, and intended merges preserve soundness.
name: GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.msmRun_preserves_sound
type:
∀ {Candidate : Type u_1} {Config : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq Candidate] (candidates : Config → Finset Candidate)
  (score : Config → Candidate → ℕ) (merge : Config → Candidate → Config) (intended : Config → Candidate → Prop)
  (Sound Complete : Config → Prop),
  (∀ (config : Config),
      Sound config →
        ¬Complete config → GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.SeparatesIntendedMerges candidates score intended config) →
    (∀ (config : Config) (choice : Candidate), Sound config → intended config choice → Sound (merge config choice)) →
      (∀ (config : Config),
          Sound config → Complete config → GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.IsMSMTerminal candidates score config) →
        ∀ {initial final : Config},
          Relation.ReflTransGen (GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.MSMStep candidates score merge) initial final →
            Sound initial → Sound final

  (∀ (config : Config) (choice : Candidate),
      GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.IsMSMChoice candidates score config choice →

docstring:
Conditional machine-independent convergence theorem for the MSM part of
Theorem 21.  The unit score gap fixes the merge order, sound intended merges
preserve the invariant, and the decreasing measure forces termination at a
complete configuration.
name: GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.theorem_21_msm_merge_order_core
type:
∀ {Candidate : Type u_1} {Config : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq Candidate] (candidates : Config → Finset Candidate)
  (score : Config → Candidate → ℕ) (merge : Config → Candidate → Config) (remaining : Config → ℕ)
  (intended : Config → Candidate → Prop) (Sound Complete : Config → Prop) (initial : Config),
  Sound initial →
    (∀ (config : Config),
        Sound config → ¬Complete config → ∃ good ∈ candidates config, intended config good ∧ 2 ≤ score config good) →
      (∀ (config : Config),
          Sound config → ¬Complete config → ∀ bad ∈ candidates config, ¬intended config bad → score config bad ≤ 1) →
        (∀ (config : Config) (choice : Candidate),
            Sound config → intended config choice → Sound (merge config choice)) →
          (∀ (config : Config),
              Sound config → Complete config → GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.IsMSMTerminal candidates score config) →
            (∀ (config : Config) (choice : Candidate),
                GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.IsMSMChoice candidates score config choice →
                  remaining (merge config choice) < remaining config) →
              ∃ final,
                Relation.ReflTransGen (GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.MSMStep candidates score merge) initial final ∧
                  Sound final ∧ Complete final ∧ GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.IsMSMTerminal candidates score final

transition-cover argument in Theorem 21: at most `m` chosen samples suffice
to exercise all `m` used transitions, and every exhaustive ordering reaches
that cover after finite time.

type:

      GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.Covers stream source →
        (∀ e ∈ used, witness e ∈ source) →
          (GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.transitionCover used witness).card ≤ used.card ∧
            (∀ e ∈ used,
                ∃ sample ∈ GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.transitionCover used witness, e ∈ exercises sample) ∧
              ∃ t, ∀ sample ∈ GenLimit.LearningAlgorithmsLimit.transitionCover used witness, ∃ n < t, stream n = sample

docstring:

boundary, not at the literal PAC/online algorithmic boundary.

type:
(∃ H, Set.Countable H ∧ GenLimit.LiRamanTewari.UniformlyGeneratable H ∧ ¬GenLimit.LiRamanTewari.PACLearnableViaVC H) ∧
  (∃ H,
      Set.Countable H ∧
        GenLimit.LiRamanTewari.OnlineLearnableViaLittlestone H ∧ ¬GenLimit.LiRamanTewari.UniformlyGeneratable H) ∧
    (∃ H,
        Set.Countable H ∧
          GenLimit.LiRamanTewari.OnlineLearnableViaLittlestone H ∧ GenLimit.LiRamanTewari.UniformlyGeneratable H) ∧
      (∃ H,
          Set.Countable H ∧
            GenLimit.LiRamanTewari.PACLearnableViaVC H ∧
              ¬GenLimit.LiRamanTewari.OnlineLearnableViaLittlestone H ∧
                ¬GenLimit.LiRamanTewari.UniformlyGeneratable H) ∧
        (∃ H,

docstring:
Claim 5.1's stabilization argument.

If the target index is active and every active index's assigned witness lies
inside its own language, then the least finite-stage eligible index eventually
stabilizes.  Its stable value is the least active index at most `z` which
contains the target and whose witness lies in the target.

  GenLimit.Generic.Presents stream (F z) →
    z ∈ I →
      (∀ i ∈ I, ↑(T i) ⊆ F i) →
        ∃ N,
          ∀ (t : ℕ),
            N ≤ t →
              GenLimit.ListIdentification.levelChoice F T I (GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t) =
                GenLimit.ListIdentification.limitChoice F T I z

docstring:
Kernel-checked form of Appendix C.3's positive-case assertion that
`A_s = {g_(2*k^n+1) | n ≥ 1} \ B(history, γ')` is nonempty.

The theorem is stronger than the source use in one respect: the finite
history may contain arbitrary standard-axis amplitudes, not only points from
the constructed support.  The hypothesis `2 ≤ k` is the nondegeneracy
condition required for the displayed power sequence to be injective; the
printed source permits `k = 1`, where that assertion fails.

∀ {t k : ℕ},
  2 ≤ k →
    ∀ (amplitudes : Fin t → ℝ) (coordinates : Fin t → ℕ) {ε' γ' : ℝ},
      0 < ε' →
        γ' < ε' →
          ∃ n,
            GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.example48G ε' (2 * k ^ (n + 1) + 1) ∉
              GenLimit.MetricSpaces.closedNeighborhood GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.hilbertDistance
                (Set.range fun i => GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.axisPoint (amplitudes i) (coordinates i))
                γ'

docstring:
Once a nondegenerate marker is forced to appear, every later
axis-supported finite history admits a fresh point of the source's optimal
reservoir.  This closes the deterministic presentation wrapper without yet
claiming the full history-dependent generator.

type:
∀ {γ γ' ε ε' : ℝ},
  γ < ε →
    0 < ε' →
      γ' < ε' →
        ∀ {stream : GenLimit.Generic.Stream ↥GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.Hilbert2}
          {L : Set ↥GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.Hilbert2} {I : Set ℕ},
          I.Infinite →
            GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.AxisSupported L →
              (∀ k ∈ I, GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.example48A ε (2 * k) ∈ L) →
                (∀ k ∈ I,
                    ∀ y ∈ L,
                      GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.hilbertDistance y
                            (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.example48A ε (2 * k)) <
                          ε →
                        y = GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.example48A ε (2 * k)) →
                  GenLimit.MetricSpaces.MetricPresentation GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.hilbertDistance γ
                      stream L →
                    ∃ T k,
                      2 ≤ k ∧
                        k ∈ I ∧
                          ∀ (t : ℕ),
                            T ≤ t →
                              GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.example48A ε (2 * k) ∈
                                  GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t ∧
                                ∃ y ∈ GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.example48Optimal ε ε' I,
                                  y ∉
                                    GenLimit.MetricSpaces.closedNeighborhood
                                      GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.hilbertDistance
                                      (↑(GenLimit.Generic.sample stream t)) γ'

    0 < r →
      GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyUnboundedSupportAt ρ r H →

docstring: Corollary 4.3 for finite-dimensional real normed spaces.

type:

  {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass E} {r δ δ' ε ε' : ℝ},
  0 < r →
    GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyUnboundedSupportAt dist r H →
      0 < δ →
        0 < δ' →
          0 < ε →
            0 < ε' →
              (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyGeneratableAt dist ε ε' H ↔
                  GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyGeneratableAt dist δ δ' H) ∧
                (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.NonuniformlyGeneratableAt dist ε ε' H ↔
                  GenLimit.MetricSpaces.NonuniformlyGeneratableAt dist δ δ' H)

docstring:

Example 4.8.

  0 < r →
    0 < ε →
      ε ≤ r →
        0 < ε' →
          ε' ≤ r →
            0 < γ →
              γ < ε →
                0 < γ' →
                  γ' < ε' →
                    GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyUnboundedSupportAt
                        GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.hilbertDistance r
                        (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.example48LanguageClass r ε ε') ∧
                      GenLimit.MetricSpaces.IsLimitGeneratorAt
                          GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.hilbertDistance γ γ'
                          (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.example48CausalGenerator ε ε' γ')
                          (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.example48LanguageClass r ε ε') ∧
                        GenLimit.MetricSpaces.GeneratableInLimitAt
                          GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.hilbertDistance γ γ'
                          (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HilbertAxisReservoir.example48LanguageClass r ε ε')

docstring:
Theorem 4.2: uniform and non-uniform generation are invariant across
positive scales on doubling spaces.
name: GenLimit.MetricSpaces.Results.theorem_4_2
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {ρ : GenLimit.MetricSpaces.Distance α} {δ δ' ε ε' r : ℝ} {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α},
  GenLimit.MetricSpaces.IsDoublingDistance ρ →
    (∀ (x : α), ρ x x = 0) →
      (∀ (x y : α), ρ x y = ρ y x) →
        (∀ (x y z : α), ρ x z ≤ ρ x y + ρ y z) →
          0 < r →
            GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyUnboundedSupportAt ρ r H →
              0 < δ →

                  0 < δ' →
                    δ' < ε' →
                      (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyGeneratableAt ρ ε ε' H ↔
                          GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyGeneratableAt ρ δ δ' H) ∧
                        (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.NonuniformlyGeneratableAt ρ ε ε' H ↔
                          GenLimit.MetricSpaces.NonuniformlyGeneratableAt ρ δ δ' H)

docstring: Repaired Theorem 4.4 under explicit mutual Lipschitz domination.

type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {ρ₁ ρ₂ : GenLimit.MetricSpaces.Distance α} {M₁₂ M₂₁ r₁ r₂ ε₁ ε₁' ε₂ ε₂' : ℝ}
  {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α},
  GenLimit.MetricSpaces.IsDoublingDistance ρ₁ →
    GenLimit.MetricSpaces.IsDoublingDistance ρ₂ →
      (∀ (x : α), ρ₁ x x = 0) →
        (∀ (x y : α), ρ₁ x y = ρ₁ y x) →
          (∀ (x y z : α), ρ₁ x z ≤ ρ₁ x y + ρ₁ y z) →
            (∀ (x : α), ρ₂ x x = 0) →
              (∀ (x y : α), ρ₂ x y = ρ₂ y x) →
                (∀ (x y z : α), ρ₂ x z ≤ ρ₂ x y + ρ₂ y z) →
                  0 < M₁₂ →
                    0 < M₂₁ →
                      GenLimit.MetricSpaces.MutuallyLipschitzDominated ρ₁ ρ₂ M₁₂ M₂₁ →
                        0 < r₁ →
                          0 < r₂ →
                            0 < ε₁ →
                              0 < ε₁' →
                                0 < ε₂ →
                                  0 < ε₂' →
                                    (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyUnboundedSupportAt ρ₁ r₁ H ↔
                                        GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyUnboundedSupportAt ρ₂ r₂ H) ∧
                                      (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyGeneratableAt ρ₁ ε₁ ε₁' H ↔
                                          GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyGeneratableAt ρ₂ ε₂ ε₂' H) ∧
                                        (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.NonuniformlyGeneratableAt ρ₁ ε₁ ε₁' H ↔
                                          GenLimit.MetricSpaces.NonuniformlyGeneratableAt ρ₂ ε₂ ε₂' H)

docstring:

docstring:

internalized at any requested positive radius.

We first refine to radius `R/4`, strictly enlarge to a pointwise `R/3`
cover, and replace every used ambient center by a point of `A` in its ball.
The resulting internal centers cover `A` at radius `2R/3 < R`.

type:

      (∀ (x y z : α), ρ x z ≤ ρ x y + ρ y z) →
        0 < r → 0 < R → GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HasFiniteCover ρ r A → GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HasFiniteInternalCover ρ R A

strongest direct conclusion supported by the repaired Theorem 4.2: its

docstring:
One doubling refinement multiplies the number of point-cover centers
by at most the displayed doubling constant.

docstring:
Theorem 3.6.  In every metric space whose whole domain has infinite
radius-`r` covering number, and at scales at most `r / 2`, there are a
uniformly generatable class and a non-uniformly generatable class whose union
is not generatable in the limit.

The witness classes are the images of Paper10's discrete Theorem 3.2 classes
inside a greedily chosen countable `r`-packing.
name: GenLimit.MetricSpaces.theorem_3_6
type:
∀ {alpha : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace alpha] {r epsilon epsilon' : ℝ},
  0 < r →
    0 ≤ epsilon →
      epsilon ≤ r / 2 →
        0 ≤ epsilon' →
          epsilon' ≤ r / 2 →
            ¬GenLimit.MetricSpaces.HasFiniteCover (fun x y => dist x y) r Set.univ →
              ∃ H₁ H₂,
                GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyGeneratableAt (fun x y => dist x y) epsilon epsilon' H₁ ∧
                  GenLimit.MetricSpaces.NonuniformlyGeneratableAt (fun x y => dist x y) epsilon epsilon' H₂ ∧
                    ¬GenLimit.MetricSpaces.GeneratableInLimitAt (fun x y => dist x y) epsilon epsilon' (H₁ ∪ H₂)

      ∀ {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α},

          GenLimit.MetricSpaces.GeneratableInLimitAt ρ₂ ε ε' H →
            GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyUnboundedSupportAt ρ₁ (r / M) H ∧
              GenLimit.MetricSpaces.GeneratableInLimitAt ρ₁ (ε / M) (ε' / M) H

docstring:
Corrected Theorem 4.4.  On two doubling genuine metrics related by
mutual global Lipschitz bounds, UUS, uniform generation, and non-uniform
generation are invariant.  All radii and novelty scales may be chosen
independently and positively on the two sides.
name: GenLimit.MetricSpaces.theorem_4_4_bilipschitz_repair
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {ρ₁ ρ₂ : GenLimit.MetricSpaces.Distance α} {M₁₂ M₂₁ r₁ r₂ ε₁ ε₁' ε₂ ε₂' : ℝ}
  {H : GenLimit.Generic.LanguageClass α},
  GenLimit.MetricSpaces.IsDoublingDistance ρ₁ →
    GenLimit.MetricSpaces.IsDoublingDistance ρ₂ →
      (∀ (x : α), ρ₁ x x = 0) →
        (∀ (x y : α), ρ₁ x y = ρ₁ y x) →
          (∀ (x y z : α), ρ₁ x z ≤ ρ₁ x y + ρ₁ y z) →
            (∀ (x : α), ρ₂ x x = 0) →
              (∀ (x y : α), ρ₂ x y = ρ₂ y x) →
                (∀ (x y z : α), ρ₂ x z ≤ ρ₂ x y + ρ₂ y z) →
                  0 < M₁₂ →
                    0 < M₂₁ →
                      GenLimit.MetricSpaces.MutuallyLipschitzDominated ρ₁ ρ₂ M₁₂ M₂₁ →
                        0 < r₁ →
                          0 < r₂ →
                            0 < ε₁ →
                              0 < ε₁' →
                                0 < ε₂ →
                                  0 < ε₂' →
                                    (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyUnboundedSupportAt ρ₁ r₁ H ↔
                                        GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyUnboundedSupportAt ρ₂ r₂ H) ∧
                                      (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyGeneratableAt ρ₁ ε₁ ε₁' H ↔
                                          GenLimit.MetricSpaces.UniformlyGeneratableAt ρ₂ ε₂ ε₂' H) ∧
                                        (GenLimit.MetricSpaces.NonuniformlyGeneratableAt ρ₁ ε₁ ε₁' H ↔
                                          GenLimit.MetricSpaces.NonuniformlyGeneratableAt ρ₂ ε₂ ε₂' H)

docstring: Corrected, concrete semantic Algorithm 1 form of Theorem 4.1.

type:

  (observed : ℕ → α),
  Monotone activeCount →
    (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ initialWeight i) →
      Function.Injective observed →
        ∀ {totalBound : ℝ},
          (∀ (n : ℕ), GenLimit.MistakeBounded.initialPrefixWeight initialWeight n ≤ totalBound) →
            ∀ (target activation budget : ℕ),
              GenLimit.MistakeBounded.FirstActivated activeCount target activation →
                (∀ (t : ℕ), observed t ∈ language target) →
                  0 < initialWeight target →
                    GenLimit.MistakeBounded.DyadicUpperBudget totalBound (initialWeight target) budget →
                      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.TotalMistakesAtMost
                        (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableTargetTrace language
                          (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticGenerated activeCount initialWeight language
                            observed)
                          target)
                        (activation + budget)

          ↑(GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount
                (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableTargetTrace language
                  (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticGenerated GenLimit.MistakeBounded.paperDoublingActiveCount
                    GenLimit.MistakeBounded.polynomialPrior language observed)
                  target)
                t) ≤
            3 * Real.logb 2 (↑target + 1) + Real.logb 2 (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6)

docstring:
The recursively maintained weights of the growing-prefix semantic run.

Indices already active at round `t` use `updateWeight`.  Newly activated

prefix through the current round is consistent with them.  Inactive indices

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight
type: {α : Type u_1} → [Infinite α] → (ℕ → ℕ) → (ℕ → ℝ) → (ℕ → Set α) → (ℕ → α) → ℕ → ℕ → ℝ

docstring:
A realizable target receives exactly its prior weight on its first
activation round.

type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (activeCount : ℕ → ℕ) (initialWeight : ℕ → ℝ) (language : ℕ → Set α)
  (observed : ℕ → α) (target activation : ℕ),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.FirstActivated activeCount target activation →
    (∀ (t : ℕ), observed t ∈ language target) →
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight activeCount initialWeight language observed activation target =
        initialWeight target

docstring:
Under a monotone schedule, every index outside the current active prefix

type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (activeCount : ℕ → ℕ) (initialWeight : ℕ → ℝ) (language : ℕ → Set α)

docstring: The weight of any active index is bounded by total active mass.

type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (activeCount : ℕ → ℕ) (initialWeight : ℕ → ℝ) (language : ℕ → Set α)
  (observed : ℕ → α),
  (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ initialWeight i) →

      target < activeCount t →

          GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableActiveWeight activeCount initialWeight language observed t

docstring: All maintained weights are nonnegative when the prior weights are.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight_nonnegative
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (activeCount : ℕ → ℕ) (initialWeight : ℕ → ℝ) (language : ℕ → Set α)
  (observed : ℕ → α),
  (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ initialWeight i) →
    ∀ (t i : ℕ), 0 ≤ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight activeCount initialWeight language observed t i

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight_succ
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (activeCount : ℕ → ℕ) (initialWeight : ℕ → ℝ) (language : ℕ → Set α)
  (observed : ℕ → α) (t i : ℕ),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight activeCount initialWeight language observed (t + 1) i =
    if i < activeCount t then
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.updateWeight
        (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight activeCount initialWeight language observed t) language
        (observed t) (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticGenerated activeCount initialWeight language observed t)
        i
    else if i < activeCount (t + 1) ∧ ∀ s ≤ t, observed s ∈ language i then initialWeight i else 0

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight_succ_new
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (activeCount : ℕ → ℕ) (initialWeight : ℕ → ℝ) (language : ℕ → Set α)

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight_succ_new_inconsistent
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (activeCount : ℕ → ℕ) (initialWeight : ℕ → ℝ) (language : ℕ → Set α)

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight_succ_old
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (activeCount : ℕ → ℕ) (initialWeight : ℕ → ℝ) (language : ℕ → Set α)
  (observed : ℕ → α) (t i : ℕ),

        i

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight_zero
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (activeCount : ℕ → ℕ) (initialWeight : ℕ → ℝ) (language : ℕ → Set α)
  (observed : ℕ → α) (i : ℕ),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight activeCount initialWeight language observed 0 i =
    if i < activeCount 0 then initialWeight i else 0

docstring:
After activation, a realizable target's weight is exactly its prior
weight multiplied by `2` once for every target mistake.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemantic_targetWeight_eq_pow_mistakes
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (activeCount : ℕ → ℕ) (initialWeight : ℕ → ℝ) (language : ℕ → Set α)
  (observed : ℕ → α),
  Monotone activeCount →
    ∀ (target activation : ℕ),
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.FirstActivated activeCount target activation →
        (∀ (t : ℕ), observed t ∈ language target) →
          ∀ (d : ℕ),
            GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticWeight activeCount initialWeight language observed (activation + d)
                target =
              2 ^
                  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount
                    (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.traceAfter
                      (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableTargetTrace language
                        (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticGenerated activeCount initialWeight language observed)
                        target)
                      activation)
                    d *
                initialWeight target

docstring: Concrete countable-class mistake inequality after target activation.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemantic_two_pow_mistakes_mul_weight_le
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (activeCount : ℕ → ℕ) (initialWeight : ℕ → ℝ) (language : ℕ → Set α)
  (observed : ℕ → α),
  Monotone activeCount →
    (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ initialWeight i) →
      Function.Injective observed →
        ∀ {totalBound : ℝ},
          (∀ (n : ℕ), GenLimit.MistakeBounded.initialPrefixWeight initialWeight n ≤ totalBound) →
            ∀ (target activation : ℕ),
              GenLimit.MistakeBounded.FirstActivated activeCount target activation →
                (∀ (t : ℕ), observed t ∈ language target) →
                  ∀ (d : ℕ),
                    2 ^
                          GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount
                            (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.traceAfter
                              (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableTargetTrace language
                                (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableSemanticGenerated activeCount initialWeight language
                                  observed)
                                target)
                              activation)
                            d *
                        initialWeight target ≤
                      totalBound

If a point starts in the fresh candidate set but is absent after `k`
scan steps, one of the accepted earlier intersections removed it.

Algorithm 1 recurrence driven by the constructed output stream.

type:

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithmWeight_eq_zero_of_not_mem_version

type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed generated : ℕ → α) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin N),
  0 ≤ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithmWeight language observed generated t i

Algorithm 1 assigns positive weight exactly to the languages still
consistent with the observed prefix.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithmWeight_pos_iff_mem_version
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed generated : ℕ → α) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin N),

    i ∈ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteVersionIndices language observed t

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithmWeight_succ

    GenLimit.MistakeBounded.updateWeight (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithmWeight language observed generated t)
      language (observed t) (generated t) i

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithmWeight_zero
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed generated : ℕ → α) (i : Fin N),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithmWeight language observed generated 0 i = 1

docstring:
The closure-dimension component of Theorem 5.1 in zero-based Lean time:
after strictly more than `d` distinct prior examples, every output is valid.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithm_correct_after_closure_dimension
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed generated : ℕ → α) (target : Fin N),
  (∀ (t : ℕ), observed t ∈ language target) →
    Function.Injective observed →
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.IsFiniteWeightedArgmax language observed generated →
        ∀ {d : ℕ},
          GenLimit.MistakeBounded.FiniteClassClosureDimensionAtMost language d →
            ∀ (t : ℕ), d < t → generated t ∈ language target

docstring:
The critical-choice step in the proof of Theorem 5.1.  Whenever the
current consistent intersection contains an unseen point, Algorithm 1's
weighted argmax is itself an unseen point in that entire intersection.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithm_critical_choice
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed generated : ℕ → α),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.IsFiniteWeightedArgmax language observed generated →
    ∀ {t : ℕ},
      (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteClassIntersection language
              (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteVersionIndices language observed t) \
            ↑(GenLimit.Generic.sample observed t)).Nonempty →
        generated t ∈
          GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteClassIntersection language
              (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteVersionIndices language observed t) \
            ↑(GenLimit.Generic.sample observed t)

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithm_lastMistakeBefore_succ_dimension
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed generated : ℕ → α) (target : Fin N),
  (∀ (t : ℕ), observed t ∈ language target) →
    Function.Injective observed →
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.IsFiniteWeightedArgmax language observed generated →
        ∀ {d : ℕ},
          GenLimit.MistakeBounded.FiniteClassClosureDimensionAtMost language d →
            GenLimit.MistakeBounded.LastMistakeBefore
              (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteTargetTrace language generated target) (d + 1)

docstring:
On a realizable stream, the target is never eliminated; its weight
doubles exactly on the rounds when the generated point misses it.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithm_targetWeight_eq_pow_mistakes
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed generated : ℕ → α) (target : Fin N),
  (∀ (t : ℕ), observed t ∈ language target) →
    ∀ (t : ℕ),
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithmWeight language observed generated t target =
        2 ^ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteTargetTrace language generated target) t

docstring:
Natural-logarithm form of the finite-cardinality component of Theorem
5.1.  `Nat.log 2 N` is exactly `⌊log₂ N⌋` for positive `N`.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithm_totalMistakesAtMost_log_card
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed generated : ℕ → α) (target : Fin N),

docstring: The closure component gives the corrected `d+1` total-mistake bound.

docstring:
If every generated point satisfies the weighted-argmax comparison, total

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteAlgorithm_totalWeight_mono
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed generated : ℕ → α),

docstring:
The finite-class mistake inequality in Theorem 5.1:

docstring:
The full argmax rule implies the one comparison needed by the weighted

∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed generated : ℕ → α),

docstring:
The finite-class structural assumption used by Paper 29 is a sufficient

docstring:
Intersection of an indexed finite subcollection, matching Definition 4

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteClassIntersection

docstring:
The consistent intersection has an unseen point after the corrected
closure threshold.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteClassIntersection_has_fresh_after_dimension
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α),

docstring:
Once more than `d` distinct examples have been observed, the current
consistent intersection must be infinite under Definition 4's bound.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteClassIntersection_infinite_after_dimension
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α),

      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.FiniteClassClosureDimensionAtMost language d →
        d < t →
          (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteClassIntersection language
              (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteVersionIndices language observed t)).Infinite

docstring:
Algorithm 1's output stream, selecting a fresh weighted maximizer at

On an injective observed enumeration, the constructed argmax also

The constructed stream satisfies the full unseen weighted-argmax rule

docstring:
Concrete, assumption-free-in-the-generator form of the logarithmic

type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (target : Fin N),

docstring: The recursively maintained weight vector for the concrete semantic run.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteSemanticWeight

      (observed t) (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteSemanticGenerated language observed t) i

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteSemanticWeight_zero
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (i : Fin N),

docstring: Mistakes against a selected target language.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteTargetTrace
type: {α : Type u_1} → {N : ℕ} → (Fin N → Set α) → (ℕ → α) → Fin N → GenLimit.MistakeBounded.MistakeTrace

docstring:
The indices not yet eliminated by the adversarial examples strictly
before round `t`.  This is the set `C` in Algorithms 1 and 2.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteVersionIndices
type: {α : Type u_1} → {N : ℕ} → (Fin N → Set α) → (ℕ → α) → ℕ → Finset (Fin N)

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteVersionIndices_zero
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteVersionIndices language observed 0 = Finset.univ

docstring:
Finite-class specialization underlying the logarithmic part of
Theorem 5.1: with unit surviving target weight and initial mass `N`, every
prefix with `k` mistakes satisfies `2^k ≤ N`.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finite_class_halving_bound
type:
∀ {trace : GenLimit.MistakeBounded.MistakeTrace} (P : GenLimit.MistakeBounded.HalvingPotential trace) (N : ℕ),
  P.potential 0 = ↑N → (∀ (t : ℕ), 1 ≤ P.potential t) → ∀ (t : ℕ), 2 ^ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount trace t ≤ ↑N

docstring: Membership patterns realized by points outside a finite forbidden set.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.freshMembershipPatterns
type: {ι : Type u_1} → {α : Type u_2} → Finset ι → (ι → Set α) → Finset α → Finset (Finset ι)

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.freshMembershipPatterns_nonempty
type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} (active : Finset ι) (language : ι → Set α) (seen : Finset α),
  (∃ x, x ∉ seen) → (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.freshMembershipPatterns active language seen).Nonempty

docstring:
A noncomputable semantic implementation of the paper's unseen argmax,
assuming that a fresh point exists.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.freshWeightedMaximizer
type: {ι : Type u_1} → {α : Type u_2} → Finset ι → (ι → ℝ) → (ι → Set α) → (seen : Finset α) → (∃ x, x ∉ seen) → α

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.freshWeightedMaximizer_not_mem
type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} (active : Finset ι) (weight : ι → ℝ) (language : ι → Set α) (seen : Finset α)
  (hfresh : ∃ x, x ∉ seen), GenLimit.MistakeBounded.freshWeightedMaximizer active weight language seen hfresh ∉ seen

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.freshWeightedMaximizer_spec
type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} (active : Finset ι) (weight : ι → ℝ) (language : ι → Set α) (seen : Finset α)
  (hfresh : ∃ x, x ∉ seen),
  ∀ x ∉ seen,
    GenLimit.MistakeBounded.weightedScore active weight language x ≤
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.weightedScore active weight language
        (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.freshWeightedMaximizer active weight language seen hfresh)

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.geometricPrefix
type: ℕ → ℕ → ℕ

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.geometricPrefix_succ
type:
∀ (base i : ℕ),
  0 < i →
    GenLimit.MistakeBounded.geometricPrefix base (i + 1) = GenLimit.MistakeBounded.geometricPrefix base i + base ^ i

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.geometricPrefix_zero
type: ∀ (base : ℕ), GenLimit.MistakeBounded.geometricPrefix base 0 = 0

docstring:
Abstract guarded halving bound: after `k` mistakes, the initial potential
is at least `2^k` times the positive surviving weight.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.halvingPotential_bound
type:
∀ {trace : GenLimit.MistakeBounded.MistakeTrace} (P : GenLimit.MistakeBounded.HalvingPotential trace) {weight : ℝ},
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.TargetWeightSurvives P weight →
    ∀ (t : ℕ), 2 ^ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount trace t * weight ≤ P.potential 0

docstring: The semantic weighted argmax is total on every infinite point universe.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.infiniteFreshWeightedMaximizer
type: {α : Type u_1} → {ι : Type u_2} → [Infinite α] → Finset ι → (ι → ℝ) → (ι → Set α) → Finset α → α

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.infiniteFreshWeightedMaximizer_not_mem
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : Infinite α] (active : Finset ι) (weight : ι → ℝ) (language : ι → Set α)
  (seen : Finset α), GenLimit.MistakeBounded.infiniteFreshWeightedMaximizer active weight language seen ∉ seen

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.infiniteFreshWeightedMaximizer_spec
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : Infinite α] (active : Finset ι) (weight : ι → ℝ) (language : ι → Set α)
  (seen : Finset α),
  ∀ x ∉ seen,
    GenLimit.MistakeBounded.weightedScore active weight language x ≤
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.weightedScore active weight language
        (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.infiniteFreshWeightedMaximizer active weight language seen)

docstring: Prior mass assigned to a finite index prefix.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.initialPrefixWeight
type: (ℕ → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.lastMistakeBefore_implies_finite
type:
∀ {trace : GenLimit.MistakeBounded.MistakeTrace} {last : ℕ},
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.LastMistakeBefore trace last → GenLimit.MistakeBounded.FinitelyManyMistakes trace

docstring:
If no mistakes occur from round `last` onward, then there are at most
`last` mistakes in total.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.lastMistakeBefore_implies_totalMistakesAtMost
type:
∀ {trace : GenLimit.MistakeBounded.MistakeTrace} {last : ℕ},
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.LastMistakeBefore trace last → GenLimit.MistakeBounded.TotalMistakesAtMost trace last

docstring:
Full deterministic content of Lemma 6.2.

The total number of mistakes is bounded both by `2 * target` and by the
no-more-mistakes threshold from Lemma 6.3.  Their minimum is the paper's
`min {2(i - 1), max {i - 1, m(Lᵢ) + 1}}` after translating the one-based
paper index `i` to the zero-based Lean index `target = i - 1`.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.lemma_6_2_modifiedGreedy_complete
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α),
  Function.Injective observed →
    ∀ (target m : ℕ),
      (∀ (s : ℕ), observed s ∈ language target) →
        GenLimit.MistakeBounded.NonuniformComplexityAtMost language target m →
          GenLimit.MistakeBounded.TotalMistakesAtMost
            (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableTargetTrace language
              (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyGenerated language observed) target)
            (min (2 * target) (max target (m + 1)))

docstring: Trace-level form of the `2(i - 1)` component of Lemma 6.2.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.lemma_6_2_modifiedGreedy_mistake_bound
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α),
  Function.Injective observed →
    ∀ (target : ℕ),
      (∀ (s : ℕ), observed s ∈ language target) →
        GenLimit.MistakeBounded.TotalMistakesAtMost
          (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableTargetTrace language
            (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyGenerated language observed) target)
          (2 * target)

docstring:
Exact semantic form of Lemma 6.3.

In zero-based notation, target index `target` is considered from round
`target`, and no mistakes occur once the round is also strictly larger than
the non-uniform complexity `m`.  Thus the no-more-mistakes threshold is
`max target (m + 1)`, corresponding to the paper's one-based
`max {i - 1, m(Lᵢ) + 1}` last-mistake bound.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.lemma_6_3_modifiedGreedy_last_mistake
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α),
  Function.Injective observed →
    ∀ (target m : ℕ),
      (∀ (s : ℕ), observed s ∈ language target) →
        GenLimit.MistakeBounded.NonuniformComplexityAtMost language target m →
          GenLimit.MistakeBounded.LastMistakeBefore
            (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.countableTargetTrace language
              (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyGenerated language observed) target)
            (max target (m + 1))

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mem_finiteVersionIndices_iff
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin N),
  i ∈ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteVersionIndices language observed t ↔ ∀ s < t, observed s ∈ language i

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mem_finiteVersionIndices_succ_iff
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} (language : Fin N → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin N),
  i ∈ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteVersionIndices language observed (t + 1) ↔
    i ∈ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.finiteVersionIndices language observed t ∧ observed t ∈ language i

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mem_freshMembershipPatterns_iff
type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} (active : Finset ι) (language : ι → Set α) (seen : Finset α) (pattern : Finset ι),
  pattern ∈ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.freshMembershipPatterns active language seen ↔
    pattern ⊆ active ∧ ∃ x ∉ seen, GenLimit.MistakeBounded.weightedMembershipPattern active language x = pattern

docstring:
Exact representation of the candidate set: a point survives iff it is
fresh and belongs to every language selected so far.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mem_modifiedGreedyCandidates_iff
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (t k : ℕ) (x : α),
  x ∈ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t k ↔
    x ∉ GenLimit.Generic.sample observed t ∧
      ∀ j ∈ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedySelected language observed t k, x ∈ language j

docstring: Number of mistakes strictly before round `t`.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount
type: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.MistakeTrace → ℕ → ℕ

docstring:
Mistakes split exactly into the prefix before `activation` and the
shifted suffix.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount_add_traceAfter
type:
∀ (trace : GenLimit.MistakeBounded.MistakeTrace) (activation t : ℕ),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount trace (activation + t) =
    GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount trace activation +
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.traceAfter trace activation) t

docstring: A trace has at most one mistake per round.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount_le_round
type: ∀ (trace : GenLimit.MistakeBounded.MistakeTrace) (t : ℕ), GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount trace t ≤ t

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount_mono
type:
∀ (trace : GenLimit.MistakeBounded.MistakeTrace) {s t : ℕ},
  s ≤ t → GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount trace s ≤ GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount trace t

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount_succ
type:
∀ (trace : GenLimit.MistakeBounded.MistakeTrace) (t : ℕ),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount trace (t + 1) =
    GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount trace t + if trace t = true then 1 else 0

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount_zero
type: ∀ (trace : GenLimit.MistakeBounded.MistakeTrace), GenLimit.MistakeBounded.mistakeCount trace 0 = 0

docstring:
Candidate points after scanning the first `k` language indices at
round `t`.

The initial candidates are precisely the points not previously observed.
At step `k`, language `k` is intersected in exactly when it is
history-consistent and the proposed intersection is nonempty.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates
type: {α : Type u_1} → (ℕ → Set α) → (ℕ → α) → ℕ → ℕ → Set α

docstring: Scanning more languages can only shrink the candidate set.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates_antitone
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (t : ℕ) {k m : ℕ},
  k ≤ m →
    GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t m ⊆
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t k

docstring: Every candidate remains fresh from the observations before the round.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates_fresh
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (t k : ℕ),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t k ⊆ {x | x ∉ GenLimit.Generic.sample observed t}

docstring:
On an infinite universe the initial fresh set is nonempty, and every
accepted intersection is explicitly required to remain nonempty.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates_nonempty
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [Infinite α] (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (t k : ℕ),
  (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t k).Nonempty

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates_succ
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (t k : ℕ),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t (k + 1) =
    if
        GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyConsistent language observed t k ∧
          (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t k ∩ language k).Nonempty then
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t k ∩ language k
    else GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t k

docstring: Every scan step can only shrink the current candidate set.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates_succ_subset
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (t k : ℕ),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t (k + 1) ⊆
    GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t k

name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates_zero
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (t : ℕ),
  GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t 0 = {x | x ∉ GenLimit.Generic.sample observed t}

docstring: The observations strictly before round `t` all belong to language `i`.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyConsistent
type: {α : Type u_1} → (ℕ → Set α) → (ℕ → α) → ℕ → ℕ → Prop

docstring:
The intersection of the target with a finite collection of earlier
languages.  This is the set whose finite cardinality is measured by the
paper's non-uniform complexity `m(Lᵢ)`.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyFiniteIntersection
type: {α : Type u_1} → (ℕ → Set α) → ℕ → Finset ℕ → Set α

docstring:
If the target intersection is empty when it is considered, then the
target together with the actually selected earlier languages contains
exactly the already observed points.
name: GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyFiniteIntersection_eq_sample_of_empty
type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α) (target t : ℕ),
  (∀ (s : ℕ), observed s ∈ language target) →
    ¬(GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyCandidates language observed t target ∩ language target).Nonempty →
      GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyFiniteIntersection language target
          (GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedySelected language observed t target) =
        ↑(GenLimit.Generic.sample observed t)

docstring:
Exact Section 6.2 charging step.

If the target is `i`, the presentation is injective and target-consistent,
and Modified-Greedy makes a mistake at a round `t ≥ i`, then some earlier
language `j < i` was consistent with every observation before `t` but
rejects the new observation at `t`.  It is therefore permanently eliminated
at that round.

type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Infinite α] (language : ℕ → Set α) (observed : ℕ → α),

    ∀ (target : ℕ),

        ∀ (t : ℕ),
          target ≤ t →
            GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyGenerated language observed t ∉ language target →
              ∃ j < target,
                GenLimit.MistakeBounded.modifiedGreedyConsistent language observed t j ∧ observed t ∉ language j
